- First-party BIC page https://github.com/Roskus/prospero-flow-crm/commit/e3c6897d0cdd1e61ff74ba5221dac0faa6c689f2 and local git show establish that e3c6897d0cdd1e61ff74ba5221dac0faa6c689f2 added app/Http/Controllers/Api/Transaction/TransactionReadController.php with public function read(int $id) and $transaction = Transaction::find($id), and added Route::get('/transaction/{id}', ...)->middleware(['auth:api']) in routes/api.php.
- git log -L over app/Http/Controllers/Api/Transaction/TransactionReadController.php traces the vulnerable method directly from its creation in e3c6897d0cdd1e61ff74ba5221dac0faa6c689f2 to its correction in 980c35ac00e419591a8adc2d1dbcc120ea62e273. git log --all --full-history --diff-filter=A reports e3c6897d0cdd1e61ff74ba5221dac0faa6c689f2 as the sole addition of that path, and git log --all -S for Route::get('/transaction/{id}' likewise reports that commit. It is an ordinary one-parent feature commit, not a move, revert, backport, or observable squash requiring decomposition.

### 43. GHSA-xrvm-rxhf-gwgp — `alias-83a85ace9f3173db55bebf57`

- Repository: `roskus/prospero-flow-crm`
- Official IDs: `CVE-2026-19734`, `GHSA-xrvm-rxhf-gwgp`

- Verdict: **NOT_AI**

**Vulnerability semantics.** The product edit and save paths trusted a user-controlled numeric product ID without binding the lookup to Auth::user()->company_id. GET /product/update/{id} loaded Product::find($id) and rendered the record's commercial fields, while POST /product/save loaded Product::find($data['id']) and then overwrote that record's company_id with the attacker's company, allowing an authenticated tenant to disclose and take over another tenant's product. ProductUpdateController and ProductCreateController also did not inherit MainController, so they did not receive its auth and locked middleware.

**Flaw origin.** Commit 0a2eeb13e0a020bc59c7622527c49a15087869da first wrote both identifier-trusting operations in app/Http/Controllers/ProductController.php: Product::find($id) in edit() and Product::find($request->id) in save(), and made POST /product/save reachable. Its direct parent has neither method nor either lookup. Later tenancy work made those unscoped lookups cross-company: 8c661622c387b0c0a7f76ad56f545d780ebf6a91 added product.company_id without scoping the reads, and e0e204da8ca57b0865b7e5df8cd495b2bc76d6e2 assigned Auth::user()->company_id after the unscoped save lookup. c028795fe359e5eb750956325dbddae4ff567093, the 5f6379ac899e4705aba272da62582ade30a5a655 plus 9e07ae4c618e326a5af39b742e2bc0984906c28d sequence, and 65f6b9f961efe533b4d3f20f1eddad132fe8ef1d subsequently relocated or reconstituted the same flawed operations and therefore are not BICs.

**Fix.** fix `f36c2a115f4c28c82181f1798c01582ae953b932`; direct fix `f36c2a115f4c28c82181f1798c01582ae953b932`.

Commit 33a30a5d0de8714198b063742405aa82ae9abda6 simultaneously made the disclosure and creation paths operative: it added the unscoped period_year listing and rendered sensitive fields, created the global exists:user,id rule, and persisted that validated foreign key.

### 46. GHSA-4gcc-rqqq-58jp — `alias-add280c86822d750a1d30572`

- Repository: `gitlab.freedesktop.org/xorg/xserver`
- Official IDs: `CVE-2026-56000`, `GHSA-4gcc-rqqq-58jp`
- Selection: status `UNANALYZED`; score `166.0`; signals `repo_ai_commit_scan, ai_commits:128, unreviewed_advisory, ghsa_bundle, 2026`.
- Reproduction: bundle `.ai-slop/state/research-queue/round10/case-alias-add280c86822d750a1d30572.json`; SHA-256 `a3a977461d8dfcf5541e38fab0f7dae5aae4ddffc9e0cccf9b1ba38da02122b2`; base revision `1`; raw result `research/round10-top200-20260828/primary/w045.json`.
- Verdict: **NOT_AI**

**Vulnerability semantics.** In glx/vndcmds.c, CommonMakeCurrent() obtains oldTag as a direct pointer into a client's cl->contextTags array through GlxLookupContextTag(). When all 16 initial tag slots are occupied, the nested CommonMakeNewCurrent() -> GlxAllocContextTag() path in glx/vndservermapping.c grows that array with realloc(), which can free and move the allocation. The vulnerable ordering then calls GlxFreeContextTag(oldTag) through the stale pointer and zeros fields in freed heap memory. An authenticated local X client can reach the write by creating 17 GLX contexts, filling the first 16 tags with MakeCurrent(oldContextTag=0), and switching to the seventeenth with a nonzero oldContextTag so allocation occurs while oldTag is retained.

**Flaw origin.** Commit 4781f2a5a8c2c2b000374e2d87982a6701d5a6b3 tried to preserve the old context tag when CommonMakeNewCurrent() fails. It removed GlxFreeContextTag() from CommonLoseCurrent() and moved that free to after CommonMakeNewCurrent() succeeds, but did not account for GlxAllocContextTag() reallocating the same array that owns oldTag. That focused ordering change first created the dangling-pointer write; it was not a move, refactor, merge, release commit, or squash aggregate.

**BIC lifecycle.** introducer `4781f2a5a8c2c2b000374e2d87982a6701d5a6b3`; parent `3852b0d10a061348ea8214fbcbef3c5c08cac0b6`; parent absence verified `True`; squash decomposed `False`; members `[]`.

**AI marker on BIC.** absent — the exact commit object for 4781f2a5a8c2c2b000374e2d87982a6701d5a6b3 names human author Doğukan Korkmaztürk <dkorkmazturk@nvidia.com>, human committer Olivier Fourdan <fourdan@gmail.com>, and only the trailer Signed-off-by: Doğukan Korkmaztürk <dkorkmazturk@nvidia.com>; it contains no Co-Authored-By, Generated-with, Assisted-by, bot identity, or other AI marker.

**Fix.** fix `2779affbdb4354e894f490e56f962527d6125043`; direct fix `2779affbdb4354e894f490e56f962527d6125043`.

**Reviewer-ready evidence.**

- First-party X.Org security advisory forwarded by X.Org maintainer Peter Hutterer at https://www.openwall.com/lists/oss-security/2026/07/08/2 identifies CVE-2026-56000/ZDI-CAN-30561, describes the retained cl->contextTags pointer, realloc-triggering 17th MakeCurrent request, stale GlxFreeContextTag() write, and names fixed releases xorg-server-21.1.24 and xwayland-24.1.13. It also expressly says the report against 21.1.16 could not be reproduced, the flaw is present on main/discontinued master and Xwayland, and 21.1.x distributions that backported 4781f2a5a8c2c2b000374e2d87982a6701d5a6b3 are definitely affected.

### 47. GHSA-jx39-26rr-cwqp — `alias-c2fbc2a6e069b24b0b2da43e`

- Repository: `gitlab.freedesktop.org/xorg/xserver`
- Official IDs: `CVE-2026-50262`, `GHSA-jx39-26rr-cwqp`

- Reproduction: bundle `.ai-slop/state/research-queue/round10/case-alias-c2fbc2a6e069b24b0b2da43e.json`; SHA-256 `17262673fefd7a4d9360d7893c1150883f1bd61466027e8525997e5cb7e43ce4`; base revision `1`; raw result `research/round10-top200-20260828/primary/w046.json`.
- Verdict: **NOT_AI**

**Vulnerability semantics.** A local GLX client can send ChangeDrawableAttributes with a request buffer shorter than the numAttribs count claims. Both native and byte-swapped dispatchers compute the required size but compare it in the wrong direction: expected_words < client->req_len. That rejects an overlong request while allowing an undersized one. The native dispatcher then passes req + 1 to DoChangeDrawableAttributes, whose numAttribs loop reads two CARD32 values per claimed attribute beyond the request buffer, disclosing adjacent server memory; the byte-swapped path first swaps the same client-controlled number of words in place, providing an out-of-bounds write path for byte-swapped clients, which the advisory says are disabled by default.

**Flaw origin.** Commit 402b329c3aa8ddbebaa1f593306a02d4cd6fed26 deliberately replaced REQUEST_FIXED_SIZE in glx/glxcmds.c and glx/glxcmdsswap.c with a Mesa compatibility workaround. For ChangeDrawableAttributes it wrote the manual '< client->req_len' comparison, reversing the required rejection condition and creating the undersized-request bypass. The immediate parent used the correct REQUEST_FIXED_SIZE macro in both dispatchers.

**BIC lifecycle.** introducer `402b329c3aa8ddbebaa1f593306a02d4cd6fed26`; parent `1137c11be0f82049d28024eaf963c6f76e0d4334`; parent absence verified `True`; squash decomposed `False`; members `[]`.

**AI marker on BIC.** absent: the exact BIC commit object for 402b329c3aa8ddbebaa1f593306a02d4cd6fed26 has human author and committer Julien Cristau <jcristau@debian.org>; its only trailers are Reported-by, Signed-off-by, and Reviewed-by. It has no Co-Authored-By, Generated-with, Assisted-by, AI-tool trailer, or bot identity.

**Fix.** fix `6d459e4daf715bea8abdafa8fb130be2f8a1d145`; direct fix `6d459e4daf715bea8abdafa8fb130be2f8a1d145`.

**Reviewer-ready evidence.**

- The first-party X.Org advisory at https://lists.x.org/archives/xorg-announce/2026-June/003702.html identifies the GLX ChangeDrawableAttributes out-of-bounds read/write, says the write requires byte-swapped clients, states that X.Org Server before 21.1.23 and Xwayland before 24.1.12 are affected, and links the direct fix https://gitlab.freedesktop.org/xorg/xserver/-/commit/6d459e4daf715bea8abdafa8fb130be2f8a1d145 (merged through first-party MR https://gitlab.freedesktop.org/xorg/xserver/-/merge_requests/2228). The fix message itself names 402b329c3aa8ddbebaa1f593306a02d4cd6fed26 as the commit being effectively reverted. In the clone, git log -L 1501,1514:glx/glxcmds.c at the BIC and git log -S client->req_len over parent..BIC both identify only 402b329c3aa8ddbebaa1f593306a02d4cd6fed26 for the flawed block; the BIC is a one-parent, non-squash commit and its diff adds the same reversed check to glx/glxcmds.c and glx/glxcmdsswap.c. Direct-parent tree verification at 1137c11be0f82049d28024eaf963c6f76e0d4334 shows REQUEST_FIXED_SIZE(xGLXChangeDrawableAttributesReq, req->numAttribs << 3) at glx/glxcmds.c:1501 and glx/glxcmdsswap.c:479, so the vulnerable manual '< client->req_len' lines are absent. At the BIC, glx/glxcmds.c:1469-1488 shows DoChangeDrawableAttributes indexing attribs[i * 2] and attribs[i * 2 + 1], and glx/glxcmdsswap.c:479-483 shows the bypass followed by __GLX_SWAP_INT_ARRAY(attribs, req->numAttribs << 1). Tag ancestry places the BIC in xorg-server-1.10.0 and in all four boundary tags checked. Source-tree checks show the flawed comparator in xorg-server-21.1.22 at glx/glxcmds.c:1531-1533 and glx/glxcmdsswap.c:443-445 and in xwayland-24.1.11 at the same lines; xorg-server-21.1.23 and xwayland-24.1.12 instead contain REQUEST_FIXED_SIZE at glx/glxcmds.c:1525 and glx/glxcmdsswap.c:443. The release-branch fixes are 94341bd715d62ba8da4c1851f517018996da1af8 for xorg-server-21.1.23 and 901da57abfde6bf2ae33859c2dd47b45d6dd5871 for xwayland-24.1.12; git patch-id --stable gives identical patch id 90e3f8d28381bc8c44e9446345e273f877cdaa9f for both and for direct fix 6d459e4daf715bea8abdafa8fb130be2f8a1d145. The BIC is available first-party at https://gitlab.freedesktop.org/xorg/xserver/-/commit/402b329c3aa8ddbebaa1f593306a02d4cd6fed26.

**Reasoning.** The vulnerability is not the original attribute loop by itself: before the BIC, both dispatchers coupled numAttribs to the actual request length with REQUEST_FIXED_SIZE. The 2011 Mesa workaround is the smallest causal change because it alone disabled that correct check and introduced the reversed manual comparison in both externally reachable dispatch paths; git history traces those exact lines to that commit, and the immediate parent proves they were absent while the safe macro was present. The BIC predates and is an ancestor of the vulnerable release boundaries, while the direct fix restores REQUEST_FIXED_SIZE and patch-equivalent backports are present in exactly the first fixed X.Org Server and Xwayland tags named by the advisory. AI attribution is judged only from the BIC commit object. Its human identities and trailers contain no AI marker, so the causal verdict is NOT_AI; the Assisted-by marker on the 2026 fix is irrelevant to attribution of the 2011 BIC.

### 48. GHSA-4ph5-83mw-vm42 — `alias-dce0bce1305aaf4c0414a565`

- Verdict: **NOT_AI**

**Vulnerability semantics.** CreateSaverWindow() snapshots the screen-saver private pointer in the local pPriv via SetupScreen(). After SetAttributes creates pPriv and a first forced saver creates its window, UnsetAttributes clears pPriv->attr. A second forced saver frees the old window, clears pPriv->hasWindow, and calls CheckScreenPrivate(); with attr and events NULL, hasWindow false, and installedMap None, that helper frees pPriv and clears the screen-private slot. CreateSaverWindow() nevertheless retains the non-NULL dangling local and immediately reads pPriv->attr, producing a client-triggerable use-after-free read and potential information disclosure.

**Flaw origin.** Commit 9508a382f8a9f241dab097d921b6d290c1c3a776 is the earliest and smallest commit in the repository history that adds Xext/saver.c and writes the complete flawed lifetime pattern: the SetupScreen local, CheckScreenPrivate's conditional free, CreateSaverWindow's CheckScreenPrivate call followed by reuse of the stale local, and UnsetAttributes clearing attr. Pickaxe/history tracing reaches this file-addition commit; later changes that blame the formatted lines are style-only rewrites. Its direct parent ded6147bfb5d75ff1e67c858040a628b61bc17d1 has no Xext/saver.c entry.

**BIC lifecycle.** introducer `9508a382f8a9f241dab097d921b6d290c1c3a776`; parent `ded6147bfb5d75ff1e67c858040a628b61bc17d1`; parent absence verified `True`; squash decomposed `False`; members `[]`.

**Reviewer-ready evidence.**

- The first-party X.Org advisory at https://lists.x.org/archives/xorg-announce/2026-June/003702.html describes the CreateSaverWindow use-after-free information disclosure, identifies ZDI-CAN-30168, states that releases before xorg-server 21.1.23 and Xwayland 24.1.12 are affected, and names https://gitlab.freedesktop.org/xorg/xserver/-/commit/ecc634f1b2f7aa473d3a267eada98c4918bf9e05 as the fix.
- The direct fix ecc634f1b2f7aa473d3a267eada98c4918bf9e05 (parent 6d459e4daf715bea8abdafa8fb130be2f8a1d145) documents the four-request sequence SetAttributes, ForceScreenSaver(Active), UnsetAttributes, ForceScreenSaver(Active). Its Xext/saver.c patch re-fetches pPriv with GetScreenPrivate(pScreen) immediately after CheckScreenPrivate(), so a freed private becomes NULL before the pPriv->attr test; it also nulls pPriv after the analogous ScreenSaverFreeAttr call.
- At 9508a382f8a9f241dab097d921b6d290c1c3a776, Xext/saver.c:232 defines SetupScreen as a local pPriv snapshot; lines 278-290 show CheckScreenPrivate freeing pPriv and clearing the screen slot when attr/events/window/map state is empty; lines 531-560 show CreateSaverWindow clearing hasWindow, calling CheckScreenPrivate, and then dereferencing the unchanged local in the pPriv->attr test; lines 1194-1211 show ProcScreenSaverUnsetAttributes setting attr to NULL.

### 49. GHSA-4r2h-m6wp-gxg9 — `alias-e45f8ec95efd4ea332bbdf89`

- Repository: `gitlab.freedesktop.org/xorg/xserver`
- Official IDs: `CVE-2026-50261`, `GHSA-4r2h-m6wp-gxg9`
- Selection: status `UNANALYZED`; score `166.0`; signals `repo_ai_commit_scan, ai_commits:128, unreviewed_advisory, ghsa_bundle, 2026`.
- Reproduction: bundle `.ai-slop/state/research-queue/round10/case-alias-e45f8ec95efd4ea332bbdf89.json`; SHA-256 `f0afd3ef4c8bcd95714ac53c9263e65a14aa51cf583beb71d312f3172ba1f45c`; base revision `1`; raw result `research/round10-top200-20260828/primary/w048.json`.
- Verdict: **NOT_AI**

**Vulnerability semantics.** Xext/sync.c SyncChangeCounter walks a SyncCounter trigger list by caching pnext = ptl->next, then may invoke pTrigger->TriggerFired. For an XSync Await group that callback is SyncAwaitTriggerFired, which FreeResource()s the Await; FreeAwait then deletes every sibling wait-condition trigger from its SyncObject (SyncDeleteTriggerFromSyncObject, historically SyncDeleteTriggerFromCounter), unlinking and freeing list nodes that can include the cached pnext. The next loop step is therefore a use-after-free (CWE-416). A local client that places multiple Await conditions on counters, then has those counters change (including via a second client), can crash the X server or escalate if it runs as root. The 2026 patch restarts iteration from pTriglist when pnext is no longer on the list.

**Flaw origin.** The unsafe iterator and the Await-fire path that frees sibling trigger-list nodes first appear together in public xserver git as ded6147bfb5d75ff1e67c858040a628b61bc17d1 (2003-11-14, Kaleb Keithley, "R6.6 is the Xorg base-line"). That commit adds Xext/sync.c containing SyncChangeCounter's for (ptl = pCounter->pTriglist; ptl; ptl = pnext) { pnext = ptl->next; if (CheckTrigger) TriggerFired; } loop, SyncAwaitTriggerFired calling FreeResource on the Await, and FreeAwait calling SyncDeleteTriggerFromCounter for each wait condition. Immediate parent cb6ef07bf01e72d1a6e6e83ceb7f76d6534da941 has no Xext/sync.c (tree is only hw/). Later c66a410d378090f350beb398649e9d9262933785 (generic SyncObject rename), 9838b7032ea9792bec21af424c53c07078636d21 (indent-only), 2523a445a09a75a8baf642608d099a5e12d5437f (SyncUpdateCounter split), and e0f872207aa203adb85e825c311ed50fe3a3af60 (CARD64 to int64_t) keep the same pnext cache and fire path; they are not first-writes. The 2003 commit is a vendor import/baseline rather than a reconstructable squash of finer public members; no finer public object first writing these lines was found.

**BIC lifecycle.** introducer `ded6147bfb5d75ff1e67c858040a628b61bc17d1`; parent `cb6ef07bf01e72d1a6e6e83ceb7f76d6534da941`; parent absence verified `True`; squash decomposed `False`; members `[]`.

**AI marker on BIC.** absent; author Kaleb Keithley <kaleb@freedesktop.org>, committer Kaleb Keithley <kaleb@freedesktop.org>; cat-file -p shows only subject "R6.6 is the Xorg base-line" with no Co-Authored-By, Generated-with, Assisted-by, or bot identity

Pre-fix function at bdd7bf57^:Xext/sync.c ~716-728 is the pnext/TriggerFired loop. git log -L :SyncChangeCounter:Xext/sync.c traces that loop to file add ded6147bfb5d75ff1e67c858040a628b61bc17d1. git cat-file -p ded6147bfb: author/committer Kaleb Keithley, parent cb6ef07bf01e72d1a6e6e83ceb7f76d6534da941. git cat-file -e ded6147bfb^:Xext/sync.c fails (path absent); parent tree names only hw/. - Reproduction: bundle `.ai-slop/state/research-queue/round10/case-alias-f1a645cb5e3717ca4d56d24a.json`; SHA-256 `36cc1d85b8c29ddc4632aba5f453ef1f7b691f80f14e5f9c67607f54692929b9`; base revision `1`; raw result `research/round10-top200-20260828/primary/w049.json`.
- Verdict: **NOT_AI**

**Vulnerability semantics.** Xext/sync.c FreeCounter sets beingDestroyed, then walks pCounter->sync.pTriglist calling pTrigger->CounterDestroyed on each node before taking pnext and free()ing the node. For an XSync Await, CounterDestroyed is SyncAwaitTriggerFired, which FreeResource()s the Await; FreeAwait then xfree/free()s the entire SyncAwaitUnion that holds every wait-condition SyncAwait. When several Await conditions reference the same counter, FreeAwait skips SyncDeleteTriggerFromSyncObject because beingDestroyed is already TRUE, so leftover list nodes still point at the now-freed SyncAwait objects. The next loop step therefore reads ptl->pTrigger (and can also lose a valid pnext) after the backing Await memory is gone (CWE-416). A local client that awaits multiple conditions on counters and has a second client destroy those counters can crash the X server or escalate if it runs as root. The 2026 patch uses nt_list_for_each_entry_safe, advances pTriglist before the callback, guards a NULL pTrigger, and NULLs remaining list pTrigger pointers from FreeAwait while the object is being destroyed.

**Flaw origin.** The FreeCounter destroy-iteration and the Await path that frees sibling SyncAwait structs first appear together in public xserver git as ded6147bfb5d75ff1e67c858040a628b61bc17d1 (2003-11-14, Kaleb Keithley, "R6.6 is the Xorg base-line"). That commit adds Xext/sync.c with FreeCounter looping for (ptl = pCounter->pTriglist; ptl; ptl = pnext) { (*ptl->pTrigger->CounterDestroyed)(ptl->pTrigger); pnext = ptl->next; xfree(ptl); }, FreeAwait skipping SyncDeleteTriggerFromCounter when pCounter->beingDestroyed is set, SyncAwaitTriggerFired calling FreeResource on the Await, and pAwait->trigger.CounterDestroyed = SyncAwaitTriggerFired. Immediate parent cb6ef07bf01e72d1a6e6e83ceb7f76d6534da941 has no Xext/sync.c (tree is only hw/). Later 1a99110f0c221b79045ea26d61c4a1ec1e0d7341 (ANSI prototypes), 9838b7032ea9792bec21af424c53c07078636d21 (indent), 99daf419a3070c347c0cd29b4a9bae07eca7bd6d / c66a410d378090f350beb398649e9d9262933785 (generic SyncObject), and 7f962c70b6d9c346477f23f6c15211e749110078 (wrap the same loop in if (initialized)) preserve the CounterDestroyed walk; they are not first-writes. The 2003 commit is a vendor import/baseline rather than a reconstructable squash of finer public members; no finer public object first writing these lines was found.

### 51. GHSA-gf2q-c269-pqgc — `alias-4caa37dabf3f0bfc9c9e66f7`

- Repository: `harttle/liquidjs`

- Selection: status `UNANALYZED`; score `165.925`; signals `repo_ai_commit_scan, ai_commits:23, reviewed_advisory, ghsa_bundle, 2026`.

- Verdict: **NOT_AI**

**Vulnerability semantics.** A template-controlled filter name was used as a bracket key on Liquid.filters, a normal JavaScript object. Therefore `valueOf` resolved to the inherited Object.prototype.valueOf even though no such filter had been registered. Filter.render then invoked that inherited function with an engine-owned receiver containing `context`, `liquid`, and, in later versions, `token`; valueOf returned the receiver itself. A crafted template could retain that object, traverse the leaked Liquid engine to its parser/loader/options/filesystem and filter registry, and use the advisory's group_by/where/comparable gadgets to obtain Function and invoke child_process, producing remote code execution. The analogous inherited lookup on Liquid.tags also let names such as `constructor` bypass the unknown-tag check. The fix makes both registries null-prototype objects so inherited Object.prototype members cannot resolve.

**Flaw origin.** The plain-object filter registry predated the vulnerability and the direct parent invoked filters with only a Context receiver. Commit f9f595f0f4604bfcfeabe097a01c6df6eb98baed is the smallest non-refactor commit that made the advisory's RCE-enabling leak: it deliberately threaded the complete Liquid instance through FilterMap/Value/Filter and changed src/template/filter/filter.ts from `this.impl.apply({ context }, ...)` to `this.impl.apply({ context, liquid: this.liquid }, ...)`. Because the inherited valueOf lookup already existed, that one focused feature commit made an unregistered template filter return a receiver containing the parser, filter registry, and filesystem-bearing engine. Later token exposure and group_by/where gadgets expanded or operationalized the attack but did not originate the privileged engine leak.

**BIC lifecycle.** introducer `00bc1efe6a514b24b0bfc2e4196ab2211e7d9fa8`; parent `6fb47962021bcf5ade0e2b7733883e6690da4df3`; parent absence verified `False`; squash decomposed `False`; members `[]`.

**Fix.** fix `457fae0736c3ec862539b9dbf7f477e6c08fb6c6`; direct fix `457fae0736c3ec862539b9dbf7f477e6c08fb6c6`.

The maintainer's first-party fix thread https://github.com/harttle/liquidjs/issues/897 states the exact root cause: `liquid.filters` and `liquid.tags` were plain `{}` objects; template-controlled bracket access inherited Object.prototype; src/template/filter.ts invoked the selected handler as `this.handler.apply({ context, token, liquid }, ...)`; and src/liquid.ts should use Object.create(null). Direct-parent verification at 2bbf50171be0ed484d9cb333f7d5a5dfca167486 shows src/template/filter/filter.ts still called `this.impl.apply({ context }, ...)`, Filter had no Liquid field or constructor argument, FilterMap accepted no Liquid instance, and src/liquid.ts constructed FilterMap with only strictFilters; thus the engine-leaking RCE mechanism is absent in the direct parent even though the older plain registry remains. ### 52. GHSA-hh27-hf48-9f5q — `alias-655bcbc8235a38e79d9d2d02`

- Repository: `harttle/liquidjs`
- Official IDs: `CVE-2026-45357`, `GHSA-hh27-hf48-9f5q`
- Selection: status `UNANALYZED`; score `165.925`; signals `repo_ai_commit_scan, ai_commits:23, reviewed_advisory, ghsa_bundle, 2026`.
- Reproduction: bundle `.ai-slop/state/research-queue/round10/case-alias-655bcbc8235a38e79d9d2d02.json`; SHA-256 `9c9ad8d970d78e86cb60567c5b60d9885472f5706947d5f4bee932637c580be9`; base revision `1`; raw result `research/round10-top200-20260828/primary/w051.json`.
- Verdict: **NOT_AI**

**Vulnerability semantics.** An attacker-influenced date-format argument can contain an arbitrarily large numeric strftime width such as %5000000d. The strftime parser captures that width, forwards it without a bound or resource charge to padStart(), and the historical pad() implementation prepends one character per iteration. A tiny template therefore drives attacker-sized output, repeated string copying, CPU consumption, and possible OOM while bypassing configured memoryLimit accounting and renderLimit checkpoints.

**Flaw origin.** Commit ba5ff3f41c61acc2c3668ae2bbcc48dd168b1759 added full strftime width syntax in src/util/strftime.ts: rFormat began capturing (\d+)?, format() assigned the capture to padWidth, and padStart(ret, padWidth, padChar) consumed it unchecked. The same commit refactored src/util/underscore.ts into a generic pad() whose while (n-- > 0) loop repeatedly concatenated strings. The existing src/builtin/filters/date.ts passed its format argument to strftime, while src/template/filter/filter.ts evaluated filter arguments against Context, completing the attacker-controlled path.

**BIC lifecycle.** introducer `ba5ff3f41c61acc2c3668ae2bbcc48dd168b1759`; parent `c69ad538d48f3cd52c6147da653b9d3e47dfd043`; parent absence verified `True`; squash decomposed `False`; members `[]`.

**AI marker on BIC.** absent: the exact BIC commit object names author harttle <yangjvn@126.com> and committer harttle <yangjvn@126.com>; its subject/body contain no Co-Authored-By, Generated-with, AI-tool, or bot trailer/marker.

**Fix.** fix `3129d46dc95efa357b00e5a57ee1af80a13d72ed`; direct fix `3129d46dc95efa357b00e5a57ee1af80a13d72ed`.

**Reviewer-ready evidence.**

- First-party advisory https://github.com/harttle/liquidjs/security/advisories/GHSA-hh27-hf48-9f5q identifies the unchecked numeric width path through src/util/strftime.ts to padStart()/pad() in src/util/underscore.ts, demonstrates {{ d | date: f }} with f=%5000000d exceeding memoryLimit and renderLimit, and declares affected versions <=10.25.7.
- git log -L 133,147:src/util/strftime.ts at pre-fix commit 5b9c3469085e01c79e2d0af28e2a13f730e1793d traces the vulnerable width destructuring, padWidth assignment, and padStart call to ba5ff3f41c61acc2c3668ae2bbcc48dd168b1759; git log -S'let padWidth = width' independently identifies that commit as the original addition rather than later type/refactor commits.
- The BIC diff at https://github.com/harttle/liquidjs/commit/ba5ff3f41c61acc2c3668ae2bbcc48dd168b1759 adds const rFormat = /%([-_0^#:]+)?(\d+)?([EO])?(.)/, passes width through format(), computes padWidth = width || padWidths[conversion] || 0, calls padStart(ret, padWidth, padChar), and introduces the generic per-character pad() loop in src/util/underscore.ts.
- Direct-parent tree verification of c69ad538d48f3cd52c6147da653b9d3e47dfd043:src/util/strftime.ts shows only /%./g parsing at lines 166-182 and fixed-width conversion helpers; it has no numeric-width capture, no width/padWidth variables, and no path from a format width to padStart. Thus the vulnerable lines/mechanism are absent in the immediate parent.
- At the BIC, src/builtin/filters/date.ts directly calls strftime(date, arg), and src/template/filter/filter.ts evaluates each filter argument with Expression(arg).evaluate(context), proving that a context-controlled format reaches the newly added width parser rather than merely an internal hard-coded caller.
- Tag-boundary history shows ba5ff3f41c61acc2c3668ae2bbcc48dd168b1759 first contained by v9.6.0 (tag commit 5ec3f95317e78a1d0ae8866c7f8cbf18ea8a9263); the v9.5.0-to-v9.6.0 diff adds the width regex and unchecked padWidth flow, while v9.5.0 (90d78ae6d573e977478920f81d2af0a56da88011) lacks it. The mechanism persists through v10.25.7 (34877950bfd0f88666f4ef61f7704defdea546b0), consistent with the advisory's upper bound; repository history therefore supplies the more precise lower boundary v9.6.0.
- Advisory-linked fix https://github.com/harttle/liquidjs/commit/3129d46dc95efa357b00e5a57ee1af80a13d72ed directly threads Context.memoryLimit from src/filters/date.ts into strftime, charges Number(padWidth)-ret.length before padding in src/util/strftime.ts, and replaces src/util/underscore.ts's repeated one-character loop with ch.repeat(n) plus one concatenation.
- git tag --contains 3129d46dc95efa357b00e5a57ee1af80a13d72ed starts at v10.26.0 and excludes v10.25.7. The first-party v10.26.0 release at https://github.com/harttle/liquidjs/releases/tag/v10.26.0 explicitly lists this full fix commit; the v10.26.0 tree contains the pre-allocation memory charge and the tag points to c20c0af02d33e8d2ca6b08925eadca8755257c39. Although the advisory UI says 'Patched versions None', its <=10.25.7 range, fix reference, release note, and tag-tree content prove v10.26.0 as the repository's fixed boundary.
- Exact BIC-object inspection (git show --format=raw ba5ff3f41c61acc2c3668ae2bbcc48dd168b1759) shows one parent, human author/committer harttle <yangjvn@126.com>, and no trailers or AI markers. AI attribution was decided solely from this BIC object; no squash decomposition was needed.

**Reasoning.** The causal defect begins when ba5ff3f41c61acc2c3668ae2bbcc48dd168b1759 makes decimal width text in a date format control the number of padding iterations with no bound. Earlier fixed-width padStart calls are not the same vulnerability: the immediate parent cannot parse %5000000d as a width, whereas the BIC both recognizes the width and routes it into the concatenating loop. Context-evaluated filter arguments make that new data flow reachable from attacker-influenced render data. The vulnerable flow survives later moves and refactors and is present at v10.25.7. Commit 3129d46dc95efa357b00e5a57ee1af80a13d72ed is the direct remediation because it charges the requested padding before allocation and removes per-character concatenation; it first ships in v10.26.0. The BIC is a single-parent ordinary commit, not a move, revert, merge, release commit, or squash aggregate requiring decomposition. Its exact commit object has human identities and no AI marker, so the closed causal verdict is NOT_AI even though AI signals on any later commit would be irrelevant.

### 53. GHSA-wmfp-5q7x-987x — `alias-6ec2fa3d32afe4892ec0c1f6`

- Verdict: **NOT_AI**

**Vulnerability semantics.** For layout, render, and include lookups, LiquidJS treated the configured root/partials/layouts directories as a filesystem boundary but its final Node fallback called require.resolve(file) and yielded the returned absolute path without applying the containment check used for ordinary candidates. An attacker who controls template text or, with the default dynamicPartials=true, a partial-name variable can therefore supply an absolute or traversing path; if require.resolve resolves it, Loader.lookup accepts and reads a file outside the configured directories.

**Flaw origin.** Commit 2dd43559b585fe42069e94197fb5aa2ee32ad616 introduced the mechanism itself: src/fs/node.ts added a fallback that returns require.resolve(file), src/fs/ifs.ts exposed that fallback, and src/liquid.ts appended its result directly to the candidate paths with no root validation. Later commits 24f534608489fccc155f30bbaf37397c46278da6 and b9ae479b653a34fadb98c324c4683dd1fdd31af1 only moved the same unguarded fallback into lookupFiles() and then src/fs/loader.ts; a3455ebd0b207141c34630c0af44d917db2ca1dd added containment to ordinary partial/layout candidates but left the fallback bypass intact.

**BIC lifecycle.** introducer `2dd43559b585fe42069e94197fb5aa2ee32ad616`; parent `5492fb0b173f8989d6c237883c374e271d2adb4d`; parent absence verified `True`; squash decomposed `False`; members `[]`.

**AI marker on BIC.** absent: the exact BIC commit object names author harttle <yangjvn@126.com> and committer harttle <yangjvn@126.com>; its complete message is 'feat: support require.resolve for lookup, see #168' and contains no Co-Authored-By, Generated-with, bot identity, AI reference, or other trailer.

### 54. GHSA-mmg9-6m6j-jqqx — `alias-88ea40d7bda50c6eef26d00b`

- Repository: `harttle/liquidjs`

- Verdict: **NOT_AI**

**Vulnerability semantics.** With a finite memoryLimit and attacker-controlled template content, the replace filter accounts only for input-sized data before executing str.split(pattern).join(replacement). If a short pattern occurs many times and replacement is long, the output is approximately occurrence_count * replacement.length while Limiter.use() sees only str.length (at introduction, later str.length + pattern.length + replacement.length). Because src/util/limiter.ts is only an accumulator checked at use() time and performs no post-allocation validation, the rendered string can exceed the configured limit by orders of magnitude and exhaust process memory.

**Flaw origin.** The reconstructable PR member 4395697adb63675d75e2db54bea5b4b4b00671dc first introduced memoryLimit and coupled src/filters/string.ts replace to it, but charged only str.length before the pre-existing split/join expansion. The later 94440a065333c78dee461af0049dd712c35f9e45 changed that charge to the sum of the three inputs, which is the exact expression quoted by the advisory, but preserved rather than introduced the causal input-accounting flaw.

**BIC lifecycle.** introducer `e443068cb9281883ff0fe9f755a15f52ada4e7e2`; parent `fad00aa14e8beac0514ec4196944b33276f1ff2c`; parent absence verified `False`; squash decomposed `True`; members `["68142d2377b799bcb2c30c959389e3bd4956dc23", "4395697adb63675d75e2db54bea5b4b4b00671dc"]`.

### 55. GHSA-rv5g-f82m-qrvv — `alias-a21a3d7c8ccdfc525f5c55cb`

**Vulnerability semantics.** With ownPropertyOnly=true, ordinary scope reads reject prototype-inherited keys in src/context/context.ts:readJSProperty, but sort_natural's property comparator read lhs[propertyString] and rhs[propertyString] directly. JavaScript bracket lookup therefore traversed each item's prototype. An untrusted template author could place chosen own-property probes around a target, observe the rendered sorted order, and refine probe values to recover a prototype-inherited secret through a sorting side channel. The pre-fix sort filter already used Context._getFromScope; the directly vulnerable read was sort_natural's comparator.

**Flaw origin.** e6f5f1cd853c8f7fd615937024b5dfeb3da39cf8 first added and registered sort_natural in src/builtin/filters/math.ts for issue #132. Its comparator introduced caseInsensitiveCmp(lhs[property], rhs[property]), bypassing the context property-reader abstraction. Later comparator renames, export changes, and the 7dfb620d30f8818685e1cfb8e7492313a0d036ab move to src/builtin/filters/array.ts preserved that direct lookup; ff112a4750f91475e9eccdb301d7a468e895f6ca only renamed the function to snake_case. The ownPropertyOnly security boundary arrived later in 7e99efc5131e20cf3f59e1fc2c371a15aa4109db without routing this pre-existing filter lookup through it.

**BIC lifecycle.** introducer `e6f5f1cd853c8f7fd615937024b5dfeb3da39cf8`; parent `570400ebcc80bc3a327d75744fa1a5df76adb9c1`; parent absence verified `True`; squash decomposed `False`; members `[]`.

**Reviewer-ready evidence.**

Direct-parent verification with `git show 570400ebcc80bc3a327d75744fa1a5df76adb9c1:src/builtin/filters/math.ts` shows only the existing math filters: no sort_natural/sortNatural, comparator, lhs[property], or rhs[property]. ### 56. GHSA-j5jq-cr68-v2xx — `alias-beefdc9286069a0a30206439`

- Repository: `wintercms/winter`
- Official IDs: `CVE-2026-35445`, `GHSA-j5jq-cr68-v2xx`
- Selection: status `UNANALYZED`; score `165.297`; signals `repo_ai_commit_scan, ai_commits:21, reviewed_advisory, ghsa_bundle, 2026`.
- Reproduction: bundle `.ai-slop/state/research-queue/round10/case-alias-beefdc9286069a0a30206439.json`; SHA-256 `2a3fe3ada045b7ba28c2fd8045f76a360f6603ea4d6f342ad8230784dc09e4e4`; base revision `1`; raw result `research/round10-top200-20260828/primary/w055.json`.
- Verdict: **NOT_AI**

**Vulnerability semantics.** The backend Controller accepted the form postback `_handler` field verbatim and passed it to `runAjaxHandler()`, unlike the AJAX-header path, which required an `on[A-Z][\w+]*`-shaped handler. `runAjaxHandler()` then treated a supplied name matching any controller method as a global handler and invoked it. On the Users controller's permission-free `myaccount` action, a low-privileged authenticated backend user with a valid CSRF token could therefore submit names such as `update_onDelete`, `update_onRestore`, `update_onUnsuspendUser`, or `update_onManualPasswordReset` and reach user-management methods without `backend.manage_users`.

**Flaw origin.** Commit 71a5dd67ab9e0d0da7caabd3fb5aaa3d86bb45e5 first added `modules/backend/classes/Controller.php` with the unsafe postback-to-dispatcher data flow at lines 167-170 and the unrestricted method-name fallback at lines 389-395. The framework flaw was later made directly exploitable against the built-in Users controller by 94a4ccb6abccd025e7e201590999061574ffdeb9, which deliberately set `$requiredPermissions = null` for the self-service action (then named `mysettings`, later `myaccount`). The earlier dispatcher commit is the BIC because it first wrote the root mechanism that accepted an attacker-selected non-AJAX handler name; the permission downgrade exposed that pre-existing mechanism rather than creating it.

**BIC lifecycle.** introducer `71a5dd67ab9e0d0da7caabd3fb5aaa3d86bb45e5`; parent `d412ea685560a3ce7028346d26fd9a6559eb0827`; parent absence verified `True`; squash decomposed `False`; members `[]`.

**AI marker on BIC.** absent — the exact BIC commit object identifies author and committer as `Sam Georges <sam@daftspunk.com>` and contains only the message `Welcome to the world, October :-)`; it has no `Co-Authored-By`, `Generated-with`, AI-tool trailer, bot identity, or any other trailer.

**Fix.** fix `7c2dbe04ee8d3f3ed668e9ecd167c7f115acf8fd`; direct fix `7c2dbe04ee8d3f3ed668e9ecd167c7f115acf8fd`.

**Reviewer-ready evidence.**

- First-party advisory https://github.com/wintercms/winter/security/advisories/GHSA-j5jq-cr68-v2xx describes the asymmetric validation, authenticated/CSRF-required attack, Users-controller permission downgrade, callable user-management methods, affected Composer package `winter/wn-backend-module` <=1.2.12, and patched version 1.2.13.
- At v1.2.12, `modules/backend/classes/Controller.php:320-327` reads `post('_handler')` and calls `runAjaxHandler($handler)` without validating the name, while the same file's AJAX path applies the handler-name regular expression. `modules/backend/controllers/Users.php:54-60` clears `$requiredPermissions` when the route action is `myaccount`.
- `git log -L '/Execute postback handler/,+12':modules/backend/classes/Controller.php --reverse` traces the unsafe postback block to 71a5dd67ab9e0d0da7caabd3fb5aaa3d86bb45e5; `git log --all -S"post('_handler')" -- modules/backend/classes/Controller.php` returns that same commit as the sole exact-string origin. In its tree, `modules/backend/classes/Controller.php:169` forwards the raw field and lines 393-394 call any matching controller method.
- Direct-parent verification: `git ls-tree -r d412ea685560a3ce7028346d26fd9a6559eb0827 -- modules/backend/classes/Controller.php modules/backend/controllers/Users.php` produced no entries. Thus the vulnerable Controller path and its vulnerable lines are absent from the immediate parent tree, rather than merely changed or moved there.
- The related reachability history is explicit: `git log -S'$this->requiredPermissions = null' -- modules/backend/controllers/Users.php` identifies 94a4ccb6abccd025e7e201590999061574ffdeb9 as the addition and 7f450741125f8e4d1661c81e9b2219424cf22ece as its removal. The latter creates `modules/backend/controllers/MyAccount.php` and removes the conditional permission downgrade from `modules/backend/controllers/Users.php`.
- Direct fix 7c2dbe04ee8d3f3ed668e9ecd167c7f115acf8fd changes `modules/backend/classes/Controller.php`: it adds `validateHandlerName()`, calls it before dispatching a form postback, and reuses it for AJAX. Its direct parent 7f450741125f8e4d1661c81e9b2219424cf22ece still has the raw `_handler` -> `runAjaxHandler($handler)` sequence at lines 321-324, proving this commit is the direct mechanism fix. Additional defense-in-depth in 9aabe55f9092809d5bef70d0529ef9af1a147b78 adds authorization checks in `modules/backend/models/User.php` for save/delete/restore/unsuspend/password-reset operations.

The first part is the root dispatch flaw and was present from the first addition of Backend Controller in 71a5dd67ab9e0d0da7caabd3fb5aaa3d86bb45e5; its direct parent has neither the file nor the lines. Later formatting, response-handling, and CSRF changes preserve the same raw-field data flow, so they are not introducers. Commit 94a4ccb6abccd025e7e201590999061574ffdeb9 later supplies the built-in Users reachability condition, but does not write the unsafe dispatcher. The remediation mirrors both sides of the conjunction: 7f450741125f8e4d1661c81e9b2219424cf22ece isolates My Account, 7c2dbe04ee8d3f3ed668e9ecd167c7f115acf8fd closes the root handler-name bypass, and later model guards add defense in depth. The direct fix falls between the vulnerable and patched release tags. ### 57. GHSA-m7gw-rffq-rxjm — `alias-edfe14834c31810bb774cd7d`

- Repository: `wintercms/winter`
- Official IDs: `CVE-2026-22254`, `GHSA-m7gw-rffq-rxjm`

- Verdict: **NOT_AI**

**Vulnerability semantics.** Stored cross-site scripting in the CMS Asset Manager: a backend user who has cms.manage_assets can upload an SVG containing active script. The upload handler accepts svg by extension and writes the uploaded bytes unchanged into the selected theme's web-addressable assets directory; when another user opens or embeds that stored asset, the SVG script can execute in the site's origin. The first-party advisory rates exploitation as requiring a privileged backend account and user interaction.

**Flaw origin.** Commit 71a5dd67ab9e0d0da7caabd3fb5aaa3d86bb45e5 first created modules/cms/widgets/AssetList.php. In that commit, line 56 put 'svg' in allowedAssetTypes, lines 596-598 performed only extension allowlisting, and line 603 moved the uploaded file into the theme assets path without parsing or sanitizing SVG content. This combination, not later handler renames, formatting, or the 2016 move to shared file definitions, is the smallest public-history commit that wrote the vulnerable mechanism.

**BIC lifecycle.** introducer `71a5dd67ab9e0d0da7caabd3fb5aaa3d86bb45e5`; parent `d412ea685560a3ce7028346d26fd9a6559eb0827`; parent absence verified `True`; squash decomposed `False`; members `[]`.

**AI marker on BIC.** absent — the exact commit object for 71a5dd67ab9e0d0da7caabd3fb5aaa3d86bb45e5 records author and committer as Sam Georges <sam@daftspunk.com> and message 'Welcome to the world, October :-)'; it has no Co-Authored-By, Generated-with, bot-author, or other AI trailer/marker.

**Fix.** fix `8a7f74b004fcd19721764fc63af0cdb339d9fb65`; direct fix `8a7f74b004fcd19721764fc63af0cdb339d9fb65`.

**Reviewer-ready evidence.**

Tag ancestry matches the declared boundary: the BIC is in affected releases through v1.2.9, the cited fix is absent from v1.2.9, and both the fix commit and sanitization lines are present in v1.2.10. ### 58. GHSA-f637-w7p2-m7fx — `alias-42e15310b330788c041ad6dd`

- Repository: `olivetin/olivetin`
- Official IDs: `CVE-2026-48709`, `GHSA-f637-w7p2-m7fx`
- Selection: status `UNANALYZED`; score `163.85`; signals `repo_ai_commit_scan, ai_commits:17, reviewed_advisory, ghsa_bundle, 2026`.
- Reproduction: bundle `.ai-slop/state/research-queue/round10/case-alias-42e15310b330788c041ad6dd.json`; SHA-256 `f2c56309de06d9297d438ee75ccccaa23e1d4eb701173076b698c06b69837750`; base revision `1`; raw result `research/round10-top200-20260828/primary/w057.json`.
- Verdict: **NOT_AI**

**Vulnerability semantics.** The public /api/ValidateArgumentType RPC accepted attacker-controlled binding_id and argument_name and, without calling auth.UserFromApiCall, checkDashboardAccess, or a per-action view check, looked up the server's action binding and argument configuration. With AuthRequireGuestsToLogin=true, unauthenticated callers who were denied the dashboard could still distinguish an existing binding/argument from a missing one by the RPC result (initially distinct 200 responses/descriptions, and later 200 versus CodeNotFound). Binding IDs are often predictable SHA-256 hashes of human-readable action titles, so the endpoint was an unauthenticated action/argument-enumeration oracle.

**Flaw origin.** Commit 09e1f0f984846660c8b04fda9e2f546b3f6ee40d changed the existing stateless UI helper from TypeSafetyCheck over caller-supplied value/type into binding-aware validation: it called api.executor.FindBindingByID(req.Msg.BindingId), searched binding.Action.Arguments for req.Msg.ArgumentName, returned existence-dependent responses, and called executor.ValidateArgument, but added no authentication, dashboard-access, or action-view authorization. The pre-existing unauthenticated type-only endpoint did not consult server action configuration and therefore was not yet the advisory's enumeration oracle; 09e1f0f984846660c8b04fda9e2f546b3f6ee40d is the smallest causal introducer rather than the later helper refactor or error-handling change.

**BIC lifecycle.** introducer `09e1f0f984846660c8b04fda9e2f546b3f6ee40d`; parent `5d061eb1a0ddf7649d451051d8cad5668b09b341`; parent absence verified `True`; squash decomposed `False`; members `[]`.

**AI marker on BIC.** absent: git cat-file -p 09e1f0f984846660c8b04fda9e2f546b3f6ee40d shows author jamesread <contact@jread.com>, committer jamesread <contact@jread.com>, one parent, and only the subject 'fix: Argument validation targets the bindings (fixes checkboxes, etc)'; there is no Co-Authored-By trailer, Generated-with trailer, bot identity, AI attribution, or any other trailer in the BIC commit object.

**Fix.** fix `a3865704c854061452a4ab5f6d95de3312698ccd`; direct fix `a3865704c854061452a4ab5f6d95de3312698ccd`.

**Reviewer-ready evidence.**

- First-party advisory https://github.com/OliveTin/OliveTin/security/advisories/GHSA-f637-w7p2-m7fx identifies service/internal/api/api.go:ValidateArgumentType, explains that the missing auth/dashboard check bypasses AuthRequireGuestsToLogin, documents the 200-versus-NotFound argument oracle and predictable binding IDs, and recommends adding auth.UserFromApiCall plus checkDashboardAccess.
- At 09e1f0f984846660c8b04fda9e2f546b3f6ee40d, service/internal/httpservers/frontend.go:45-64 maps public /api/<method> requests into the Connect handler; service/gen/olivetin/api/v1/apiv1connect/olivetin.connect.go:66-68 declares /olivetin.api.v1.OliveTinApiService/ValidateArgumentType and lines 555-558 bind it to svc.ValidateArgumentType. proto/olivetin/api/v1/olivetin.proto:164-171 supplies binding_id, argument_name, value, and type.
- git log -L on service/internal/api/api.go:ValidateArgumentType traces the causal addition to 09e1f0f984846660c8b04fda9e2f546b3f6ee40d. Its one-file 38-addition/1-deletion patch at service/internal/api/api.go:594-638 adds FindBindingByID, the Action.Arguments name search, existence-dependent descriptions, and executor.ValidateArgument while leaving the handler without auth.UserFromApiCall or checkDashboardAccess.
- Direct-parent tree verification: git show 5d061eb1a0ddf7649d451051d8cad5668b09b341:service/internal/api/api.go at the same ValidateArgumentType block shows only executor.TypeSafetyCheck('', req.Msg.Value, req.Msg.Type) and a Valid/Description response. It contains none of the binding lookup, action-argument search, or binding-dependent branches added by the BIC. The vulnerable mechanism is therefore absent from the immediate parent even though the harmless type-only helper itself is older.
- Lifecycle cross-check: 8e2db0ad82e73da5a2484498f79c8cfeaf88a3d9 immediately refactored the new binding-aware logic into validateArgumentTypeInternal, and bb14c5da3e64b03f207c7f38139eb60e97c278fc later made missing bindings/arguments return one CodeNotFound error. Neither removed the unauthenticated success-versus-not-found oracle, so neither is the BIC or fix.
- Attack precondition and predictability are source-backed: service/internal/api/api.go:433-438 at the BIC defines checkDashboardAccess to reject guests when AuthRequireGuestsToLogin is true, but ValidateArgumentType did not call it; service/internal/auth/authcheck.go:45-68 maps a request with no authenticated identity to UserGuest; service/internal/executor/executor_actions.go:132-148 derives an ID from action.ID or SHA-256(action.Title, optionally entity-qualified).
- Direct fix https://github.com/OliveTin/OliveTin/commit/a3865704c854061452a4ab5f6d95de3312698ccd (parent 61593a8aaf1fa1f6019e13871572d39cf2c226c6) adds auth.UserFromApiCall and checkDashboardAccess to ValidateArgumentType, then validateArgumentTypeBindingAccess/errUnlessUserMayValidateArgumentTypeForBinding with userCanViewAction enforcement in service/internal/api/api.go; it also adds regression coverage for denied guests, denied view permission, and permitted users in service/internal/api/api_test.go.
- Version boundary from repository ancestry: 09e1f0f984846660c8b04fda9e2f546b3f6ee40d first appears in stable tag 3000.8.0 (59afe01e614876a93a718f8b2e395ce38d454fd2), while 3000.7.0 (f2c3af2a2df68e915166a200f514f1feba3a10cc) has the type-only parent behavior. The fix is absent through 3000.12.0 (3c8490fa5798141f02c2e5fb2cf4c97dc074509b) and first appears in 3000.13.0 (8bf52fbea38212e269cbe82f596616b8625a562b). The first-party release https://github.com/OliveTin/OliveTin/releases/tag/3000.13.0 explicitly lists a3865704c854061452a4ab5f6d95de3312698ccd under Security.
- Advisory boundary reconciliation: the GitHub repository-advisory page displays affected <=3000.11.3 and 'Patched versions: None', but tag ancestry and source show 3000.11.4 and 3000.12.0 still contain the BIC and not the fix, while 3000.13.0 contains the fix. The GitHub advisory API record at https://api.github.com/advisories/GHSA-F637-W7P2-M7FX gives the Go-module boundary <0.0.0-20260521230847-a3865704c854 with first patched 0.0.0-20260521230847-a3865704c854, matching the fix commit's 2026-05-21T23:08:47Z timestamp and repository ancestry.
- BIC-only AI check: the exact commit object for 09e1f0f984846660c8b04fda9e2f546b3f6ee40d has human author and committer jamesread <contact@jread.com> and no trailers or bot/AI marker. No PR body, branch metadata, later refactor, or fix metadata was used for attribution.

**Reasoning.** The advisory's security boundary is not merely that ValidateArgumentType was callable without login; the endpoint became dangerous when it began consulting private server bindings and arguments and returning existence-dependent results. History separates those events cleanly. The original Connect handler and direct parent 5d061eb1a0ddf7649d451051d8cad5668b09b341 only type-checked caller-provided data. The single-parent, one-file commit 09e1f0f984846660c8b04fda9e2f546b3f6ee40d first joined unauthenticated input to FindBindingByID and Action.Arguments and exposed the result, so it is the smallest BIC; the direct-parent tree proves that mechanism absent. Later commits only moved the code or changed missing-object error behavior. The BIC lands before the earliest containing stable tag 3000.8.0, persists through 3000.12.0, and direct fix a3865704c854061452a4ab5f6d95de3312698ccd adds both the guest/dashboard gate and per-action view authorization before first fixed tag 3000.13.0. ### 59. GHSA-prj9-97mp-mwh2 — `alias-554c009134e1f17453711cbd`

- Repository: `olivetin/olivetin`
- Official IDs: `CVE-2026-53541`, `GHSA-prj9-97mp-mwh2`
- Selection: status `UNANALYZED`; score `163.85`; signals `repo_ai_commit_scan, ai_commits:17, reviewed_advisory, ghsa_bundle, 2026`.
- Reproduction: bundle `.ai-slop/state/research-queue/round10/case-alias-554c009134e1f17453711cbd.json`; SHA-256 `bf35922c02632bbbd3610d36bf0e9878303b7cbbfc9e8d52c1544b271331725f`; base revision `1`; raw result `research/round10-top200-20260828/primary/w058.json`.
- Verdict: **NOT_AI**

**Vulnerability semantics.** A user who can trigger an action can submit arbitrary StartAction argument names and values. The vulnerable filter retains every caller-controlled name beginning with `ot_`, although only `ot_executionTrackingId` and `ot_username` are legitimate system arguments and those two are overwritten by the server. Any other `ot_` name survives, is skipped by type checking because validation iterates only over the action's configured argument definitions, remains available as `.Arguments.ot_*` during template rendering, and is converted by `buildEnv` into an unvalidated uppercased environment variable for the executed command. This permits environment and template-context pollution with attacker-chosen values.

**Flaw origin.** Commit 4bbd2eab153287dc744ad061c58af7693f0c3ddc added `filterToDefinedArgumentsOnly` while fixing GHSA-49gm-hh7w-wfvf, but deliberately preserved every key with `strings.HasPrefix(k, "ot_")` so that system arguments injected before filtering would survive. That broad prefix exception, rather than an allowlist of the two server-owned keys or injection after filtering, first wrote the advisory's prefix-specific bypass. Its parent already passed all undefined arguments because it had no such filter, so this commit narrowed the older generic exposure but is still the smallest commit that introduced the exact vulnerable filter mechanism identified by GHSA-prj9-97mp-mwh2.

**BIC lifecycle.** introducer `4bbd2eab153287dc744ad061c58af7693f0c3ddc`; parent `1db6509288bb356c6b9128a2318c91fc16e80d83`; parent absence verified `True`; squash decomposed `False`; members `[]`.

**AI marker on BIC.** absent: the raw commit object for 4bbd2eab153287dc744ad061c58af7693f0c3ddc has author `jamesread <contact@jread.com>`, committer `jamesread <contact@jread.com>`, and the sole message `security: GHSA-49gm-hh7w-wfvf`; it has no Co-Authored-By, Generated-with, AI-tool, or bot marker/trailer.

**Fix.** fix `ebffd9f040f791208aee1db2e5a8aecd1e3e603d`; direct fix `ebffd9f040f791208aee1db2e5a8aecd1e3e603d`.

**Reviewer-ready evidence.**

- First-party repository advisory https://github.com/OliveTin/OliveTin/security/advisories/GHSA-prj9-97mp-mwh2 and its API record https://api.github.com/repos/OliveTin/OliveTin/security-advisories/GHSA-prj9-97mp-mwh2 identify `service/internal/executor/executor.go`: `keepArgument`/the `ot_` exception, the two-key `injectSystemArgs`, and `buildEnv`; they describe unvalidated `ot_*` arguments reaching environment variables and template context and reference fix https://github.com/OliveTin/OliveTin/commit/ebffd9f040f791208aee1db2e5a8aecd1e3e603d.

In `service/internal/executor/executor.go` lines 657-739, `stepParseArgs` injects the two known system keys before `filterToDefinedArgumentsOnly`, while the newly added conditional `if _, ok := definedNames[k]; ok || strings.HasPrefix(k, "ot_")` preserves arbitrary additional `ot_` keys.
- At that same BIC, `service/internal/executor/arguments.go` lines 85-101 validates only `req.Binding.Action.Arguments` and passes the full surviving map to `tpl.ParseTemplateWithActionContext`; `service/internal/tpl/templates.go` lines 121-140 exposes the map as `Arguments`; and `service/internal/executor/executor.go` lines 849-862 and 911 pass every map entry through `buildEnv` to the command environment.

- Direct-parent verification: 4bbd2eab153287dc744ad061c58af7693f0c3ddc has the single parent 1db6509288bb356c6b9128a2318c91fc16e80d83. `git grep -n -F 'strings.HasPrefix(k, "ot_")' 1db6509288bb356c6b9128a2318c91fc16e80d83 -- service/internal/executor/executor.go` returned no match, and the BIC diff adds the entire filter and vulnerable conditional. The parent instead had no undefined-argument filter, explaining why older releases could exhibit the broader pollution impact even though the exact prefix-exception line begins here.
- Fix verification: single-parent commit ebffd9f040f791208aee1db2e5a8aecd1e3e603d directly changes `service/internal/executor/executor.go` so `keepArgument` returns only `ok`, moves system-argument injection after filtering, validates the two system values, and adds reserved-prefix configuration validation in `service/internal/config/sanitize.go`. Its direct parent 41612c6bc6a8a6424e27e6a66fb0dae30524c768 contains `return ok || strings.HasPrefix(name, "ot_")` at line 738; the fix contains `return ok` at line 740.
- Version cross-check: the reviewed global GitHub advisory API https://api.github.com/advisories/GHSA-prj9-97mp-mwh2 declares `< 0.0.0-20260531214440-ebffd9f040f7` vulnerable and `0.0.0-20260531214440-ebffd9f040f7` first patched, exactly naming the fix commit. Repository history shows 3000.10.1 is the first tag containing the exact BIC, 3000.13.0 still has the vulnerable line, and 3000.14.0 is the first tag containing ebffd9f040f791208aee1db2e5a8aecd1e3e603d and has the fixed `return ok`; every later inspected release tag also contains the fix.

The commit and tag trees resolve the source boundary: 3000.13.0 is vulnerable and 3000.14.0 contains the direct fix; pre-BIC releases had the broader all-undefined-arguments behavior rather than the later prefix-specific filter bypass.

The password argument type was explicitly accepted without character validation, while checkShellArgumentSafety omitted password from its unsafe-type set, so shell metacharacters in a password escaped the administrator-defined command. Independently, webhook JSON extraction created arbitrary argument-name/value pairs and passed them into ExecutionRequest; names without a corresponding configured ActionArgument skipped type validation yet remained available to shell templating, allowing an unauthenticated webhook value to reach the same sh -c sink.

The direct member parent eb4f28dfdaad49e0d97dd331269dd47fb2e4d1ac had the pre-existing shell interpolation/execution path but no password special case or password UI type. A later independent origin, f22b3953b1a744fb544f27a9077d79fdb80eb242, introduced webhook extraction and forwarded the resulting unfiltered map into ExecutionRequest; its parent efa964406abec65c1707c075d7cc88b8c2a9abc8 had no service/internal/webhooks/handler.go at all.

**Vulnerability semantics.** When OAuth2 is enabled, the unauthenticated /oauth/login handler creates a state value and writes it into the handler-wide registeredStates Go map. net/http runs requests concurrently, but the map's writes and the callback/authentication reads and writes had no mutex. Parallel login requests can therefore produce Go's fatal concurrent map writes panic and terminate OliveTin remotely; callback and cookie-auth traffic supplies additional read/write race paths.

**Flaw origin.** Commit 6a7187fb5b6a7fa900d7df0f0da8fdb3ebf02734 introduced OAuth2 in internal/httpservers/oauth2.go as a new file, including the shared registeredStates map, the unlocked registeredStates[state] assignment in handleOAuthLogin, unlocked state lookups, and public /oauth/login and /oauth/callback route registration in internal/httpservers/singleFrontend.go. Its direct parent has neither the OAuth2 source file nor any registeredStates symbol. Later commit a62d58f11955fe192f45da13e23ba996a2759404 moved the same state map into OAuth2Handler, and be7c75404377ccddd07e16b57e39ead5609323f7 renamed/moved the file, but both preserved the already-vulnerable unsynchronized mechanism and are not introducers.

**BIC lifecycle.** introducer `6a7187fb5b6a7fa900d7df0f0da8fdb3ebf02734`; parent `b31cdf15a20c29f6301f02a3ba4ef97b9d99e48c`; parent absence verified `True`; squash decomposed `False`; members `[]`.

### 62. GHSA-7fq5-7wr8-rjwj — `alias-7a4c8b706a9920ea803c214c`

- Repository: `olivetin/olivetin`

- Verdict: **NOT_AI**

**Vulnerability semantics.** Concurrent action requests execute template rendering in separate ExecRequest goroutines, but the renderer calls Parse on one process-wide *text/template.Template and then executes the returned pointer, which is the same mutated receiver. Interleaved Parse and Execute operations can replace one request's parse tree with another request's tree, contaminate shell commands and arguments across users, or concurrently mutate text/template's internal maps and terminate the service.

**Flaw origin.** Commit 6b342cbedb041f515a76495cec69f9979bd34d1e first introduced the flawed Go-template mechanism in service/internal/entities/templates.go: a package-level `var tpl = template.New("tpl")`, followed on every rendering call by `t, err := tpl.Parse(source)` and `t.Execute(...)`. ExecRequest already launched each execution through `go func()`, so the new shared mutable template was immediately reachable concurrently. Later moves and refactors, including b37f035ea653e6f238a7cdfa0f636f518a692dc4, b777d599aa1869871d67eb43cf64908d513976ee, 086a5ffd22b41766f5cbe2654a53b2771fe004b7, and 544515c2a6bd44454bbdb86829e5b63da798fd71, preserved or reorganized the mechanism and are not the origin.

**BIC lifecycle.** introducer `6b342cbedb041f515a76495cec69f9979bd34d1e`; parent `17c716c599b5a11f0bb01d18827014b868a53280`; parent absence verified `True`; squash decomposed `False`; members `[]`.

**AI marker on BIC.** absent: the exact commit object for 6b342cbedb041f515a76495cec69f9979bd34d1e has human author and committer `jamesread <contact@jread.com>`, the sole message `chore: Port huge amount of code to OliveTin 3k`, no Co-Authored-By or Generated-with trailer, no bot identity, and no other AI-attribution marker.

**Fix.** fix `d74da9314005954dd49fa20dabf272247bc76519`; direct fix `d74da9314005954dd49fa20dabf272247bc76519`.

**Reviewer-ready evidence.**

- The repository's first-party advisory, https://github.com/OliveTin/OliveTin/security/advisories/GHSA-7fq5-7wr8-rjwj, identifies service/internal/tpl/templates.go, the package-level `tpl`, the unsafe `tpl.Parse(source)` then `t.Execute(...)` sequence, the ExecRequest goroutine call chain, cross-request command contamination, and concurrent-map-write denial of service. Its package panel reports affected versions `>= 3000.0.0`; although that panel currently says `Patched versions: None`, the advisory references the security fix and release, and the assigned GitHub advisory API snapshot names pseudo-version `0.0.0-20260521225117-d74da9314005` as first patched.
- First-party fix commit https://github.com/OliveTin/OliveTin/commit/d74da9314005954dd49fa20dabf272247bc76519 has parent 276e3f62ddb87f9cb87903b19203e35db01a0c95 and directly changes service/internal/tpl/templates.go: parseTemplate no longer calls `tpl.Parse(source)`; it calls `tpl.Clone()` and parses the per-call clone, so concurrent requests no longer mutate the shared root template.
- First-party release https://github.com/OliveTin/OliveTin/releases/tag/3000.13.0 explicitly lists d74da9314005954dd49fa20dabf272247bc76519 under Security for GHSA-7fq5-7wr8-rjwj. The release tag resolves to 8bf52fbea38212e269cbe82f596616b8625a562b.
- History search `git log --all -S 'tpl.Parse(source)' -- '*.go'` returns exactly the addition in 6b342cbedb041f515a76495cec69f9979bd34d1e and removal in d74da9314005954dd49fa20dabf272247bc76519. The analogous all-ref search for `var tpl = template.New("tpl")` identifies 6b342cbedb041f515a76495cec69f9979bd34d1e as its origin. `git log -L` follows the singleton through the later entities-to-tpl move and option/function refactors back to that same commit.

Thus the vulnerable shared-template lines and mechanism are absent in the immediate parent.

All-ref pickaxe searches expose no smaller member commit for the shared singleton/Parse mechanism; despite its broad port diff, no reconstructable squash-member lineage exists in the validated history, so no decomposition SHA can replace it.

There are no trailers or bot/AI markers in the commit object.

**Reasoning.** The first-party advisory and direct fix agree on the causal defect: Parse mutates a shared text/template receiver, while independent action executions can render concurrently. **Vulnerability semantics.** A privileged attacker can persist a custom RSE attribute whose key or value contains HTML/JavaScript. ### 64. GHSA-f7h5-c625-3795 — `alias-a469382c47590c70cd7abf44`

- Repository: `eclipse-ee4j/glassfish`
- Official IDs: `CVE-2024-9408`, `GHSA-f7h5-c625-3795`

- Reproduction: bundle `.ai-slop/state/research-queue/round10/case-alias-a469382c47590c70cd7abf44.json`; SHA-256 `d2e4b239ffeac209288ced5b60052ebe002a42aa83e7093a09a104f154fb784e`; base revision `1`; raw result `research/round10-top200-20260828/primary/w063.json`.
- Verdict: **NOT_AI**

**Vulnerability semantics.** A request to the Admin Console /download/log endpoint with contentSourceId=LogViewer could supply restUrl. LogViewerContentSource.getInputStream trusted that request parameter as the base URL, appended /view-log/, and issued a server-side GET; RestUtil.getRequestFromServlet also attached the authenticated session's REST_TOKEN cookie and DownloadServlet returned the fetched stream. An attacker able to drive that request could therefore make GlassFish contact arbitrary/internal hosts, observe returned content for network discovery, and potentially disclose the REST administration token to an attacker-controlled origin.

**Flaw origin.** The legacy GlassFish change for GLASSFISH-17931 created LogViewerContentSource and, in the same commit, added RestUtil.getRequestFromServlet. It made the client-controlled restUrl parameter the outbound request origin without validation or origin binding, while the helper forwarded the session REST token to that origin. The safe origin already existed as session REST_URL; the flaw was choosing request input instead.

**BIC lifecycle.** introducer `8d7b7ae8846487c31b375426c8babde8f1024f18`; parent —; parent absence verified `True`; squash decomposed `True`; members `["8d7b7ae8846487c31b375426c8babde8f1024f18"]`.

There is no Co-Authored-By, Generated-with, AI trailer, bot author, or bot committer marker.

**Fix.** fix `baa1bb56b137773a6ca921a35c60d32414a68f2f`; direct fix `baa1bb56b137773a6ca921a35c60d32414a68f2f`.

### 65. GHSA-hp97-5x6g-q538 — `alias-e9d2a63025e6f21dd728a939`

That commit newly copied FileRealm group names into a nested users map and attached it as ActionReport extraProperties. Because the pre-existing renderer traversed collections/maps and returned scalar object.toString() verbatim, this was the smallest commit that completed the advisory's specific admin-keyfile-group-to-HTML attack path.

**BIC lifecycle.** introducer `43cd2412a1bcc34d185df04d175b705ce8d38932`; parent `c9c7395474572d34fef25a9e6c8528f38a788ca0`; parent absence verified `True`; squash decomposed `True`; members `["43cd2412a1bcc34d185df04d175b705ce8d38932"]`.

Its one-file diff in v3/security/core/src/main/java/com/sun/enterprise/security/cli/ListFileUser.java adds userMap.put("groups", Collections.list(fr.getGroupNames(userName))), nests the maps in userList, and calls report.setExtraProperties(extraProperties).

### 66. GHSA-62g9-99m7-w8wv — `alias-f286a9df0245c031afbbea70`

**Vulnerability semantics.** An authenticated Administration Console user can put an HTML/JavaScript payload such as <img src=x onerror=alert(1)> into a standalone instance's ASADMIN_LISTENER_PORT system-property override. standaloneInstanceConfigProperties.jsf includes configuration/systemProperties.jsf, whose overrideVal field accepts the value, and configuration/systemPropertiesButtons.jsf posts row.overrideValue unchanged to the instance system-properties REST endpoint. When another user opens the standalone instance General Information page, the web integration reads every configured network-listener port, resolves ${ASADMIN_LISTENER_PORT} against that instance's stored system properties, joins the resolved values into pageSession.httpPorts, and supplies the result to a sun:staticText sink without requesting HTML escaping. The stored markup is therefore emitted into the victim's page and executes in the victim's authenticated browser session.

**Flaw origin.** The smallest causal change is aa41b7dcf394d495b897b8a13fa21b16e51c0c37 in the first-party predecessor repository javaee/glassfish. It added gf.resolveTokens(... endPoint=/servers/server/#{pageSession.instanceName} ...) to v3/admingui/web/src/main/resources/serverPageNode.jsf and changed the displayed list from the unresolved httpPortsList to httpResolvedPortsList. That single change connected per-instance, attacker-controlled system-property substitutions to the already unescaped staticText display. The direct parent displayed only the unresolved listener token strings, so the advisory's ASADMIN_LISTENER_PORT payload could not reach this sink there. The later 2018 Eclipse Initial Contribution is an aggregate import, and the 2017 source restructure is only a move; neither is the BIC.

### 70. GHSA-h762-gwwm-v9vj — `alias-c5bfabac9aa946a425f683f0`

- Reproduction: bundle `.ai-slop/state/research-queue/round10/case-alias-c5bfabac9aa946a425f683f0.json`; SHA-256 `f5ff32a52999a5ab388976557fe0bfc7a1d9f78e960ffb581ce869ffbcaa06d7`; base revision `1`; raw result `research/round10-top200-20260828/primary/w069.json`.
- Verdict: **NOT_AI**

**Vulnerability semantics.** A local attacker can supply a truncated/malformed IPv6 capture and run tcprewrite with --fixlen pad. tcpedit_packet derives ip6_hdr from the original packet buffer, then untrunc_packet calls realloc through safe_realloc when pkthdr->len exceeds pkthdr->caplen. If realloc moves the allocation, *pktdata is updated but tcpedit_packet's ip6_hdr alias is not. untrunc_packet returns a positive checksum-recalculation signal, so fix_ipv6_checksums later dereferences the freed IPv6-header alias (the reported read is src/tcpedit/edit_packet.c:155 in revision 6fcbf0324088561d95c356fe8337f4faac275f1a), producing a heap use-after-free and crash.

**Flaw origin.** Commit 69831b8186513309f4dd43ca5bacfc34b554ad14 changed untrunc_packet to receive u_char **pktdata and first introduced `packet = safe_realloc(packet, pkthdr->len)` for padding, but it did not refresh the caller's already-derived ip_hdr/ip6_hdr aliases after the possible move. The IPv6 checksum path already existed and continued to pass the stale ip6_hdr after untrunc_packet. Later commit 64132c54c4000046b30f1fc3fe612db9b2f26860 only enlarged the realloc request with PACKET_HEADROOM; it did not create the stale-alias mechanism.

**BIC lifecycle.** introducer `69831b8186513309f4dd43ca5bacfc34b554ad14`; parent `16abc7fe749bd3c130204d0b2707caf7cab5894e`; parent absence verified `True`; squash decomposed `False`; members `[]`.

**AI marker on BIC.** absent — the exact BIC commit object (`git cat-file commit 69831b8186513309f4dd43ca5bacfc34b554ad14`) has author and committer `Fred Klassen <fklassen@appneta.com>` and message `remalloc packets before padding to ensure not overwriting memory - closes #80`; it has no Co-Authored-By or Generated-with trailer, bot identity, AI attribution, or any other trailer.

**Fix.** fix `a93ae465b966e6f675b25564ce292fb5cfe762ad`; direct fix `73008f261f1cdf7a1087dc8759115242696d35da`.

**Reviewer-ready evidence.**

- First-party vulnerability and fix sources: https://github.com/appneta/tcpreplay/issues/972 reports the IPv6 --fixlen pad path, ASan allocation/free/read stack, revision 6fcbf0324088561d95c356fe8337f4faac275f1a, and the maintainer's 2025-08-19 statement that 4.5.2-beta3 cannot reproduce it; the same-root-cause report https://github.com/appneta/tcpreplay/issues/970 identifies realloc in untrunc_packet and the maintainer fix; https://github.com/appneta/tcpreplay/pull/975 says the buffer is already proven large enough and removes realloc; https://github.com/appneta/tcpreplay/releases/tag/v4.5.2 lists #970/#975. Source verification at reported revision: src/tcpedit/tcpedit.c:262 calls untrunc_packet with previously derived ip_hdr/ip6_hdr, src/tcpedit/edit_packet.c:562 executes safe_realloc, src/tcpedit/tcpedit.c:342 passes the unchanged ip6_hdr to fix_ipv6_checksums, and src/tcpedit/edit_packet.c:155 dereferences it; src/common/utils.c:66 shows safe_realloc invokes realloc. History verification: `git log -L '/packet = safe_realloc/,+1:src/tcpedit/edit_packet.c'` and `git log -S'packet = safe_realloc(packet, pkthdr->len'` both trace the statement's first addition to 69831b8186513309f4dd43ca5bacfc34b554ad14; its one parent is 16abc7fe749bd3c130204d0b2707caf7cab5894e, so it is an ordinary one-parent commit, not a squash requiring decomposition. Direct-parent tree verification: parent src/tcpedit/edit_packet.c:243-272 accepts u_char *pktdata and pads it directly with memset at line 271; `git grep` finds no safe_realloc in that parent, while parent src/tcpedit/edit_packet.c:85 and src/tcpedit/tcpedit.c:293 prove the IPv6 checksum function/call already existed. The BIC diff adds the realloc and **pktdata handoff without refreshing ip6_hdr, establishing parent absence of the vulnerable mechanism. Version boundaries: the BIC is contained starting at v4.0.5beta1 (and first stable v4.0.5), whereas v4.0.4 predates it; v4.5.1 still contains `packet = safe_realloc(packet, pkthdr->len + PACKET_HEADROOM)` at src/tcpedit/edit_packet.c:562. **Reasoning.** The vulnerability is created by the interaction of a moving realloc and caller-held interior aliases, not by fix_ipv6_checksums itself. Before the BIC, the same IPv6 checksum call existed, but untrunc_packet could not change the packet allocation; therefore its direct parent lacks this use-after-free mechanism. The BIC is the smallest source commit that made the packet movable during padding while retaining stale ip_hdr/ip6_hdr, and -L/-S history excludes the later PACKET_HEADROOM adjustment as merely a modification. The reported 2024 revision and v4.5.1 retain that lifecycle, while direct commit 73008f261f1cdf7a1087dc8759115242696d35da removes realloc and adds an input-length guard; merge a93ae465b966e6f675b25564ce292fb5cfe762ad lands it for the fixed release boundary. ### 71. GHSA-4cc6-crfh-q58w — `alias-d16346240cf1626f6024645d`

- Repository: `appneta/tcpreplay`
- Official IDs: `CVE-2025-8746`, `GHSA-4cc6-crfh-q58w`
- Selection: status `UNANALYZED`; score `161.0`; signals `repo_ai_commit_scan, ai_commits:102, unreviewed_advisory, ghsa_bundle, 2025`.
- Reproduction: bundle `.ai-slop/state/research-queue/round10/case-alias-d16346240cf1626f6024645d.json`; SHA-256 `01a5f6c0f179d065bbedca8f9bc8f2da5a37dceb2c2482787f82ccdb7a2b0fe4`; base revision `1`; raw result `research/round10-top200-20260828/primary/w070.json`.
- Verdict: **NOT_AI**

**Vulnerability semantics.** A local attacker can make an AutoOpts consumer such as tcpliveplay process a missing, inaccessible, empty, wrong-type, or malformed option file via --load-opts. optionProcess() then reaches optionSaveFile(), whose update/rewrite path calls open_sv_file() and remove_settings(). Vulnerable remove_settings() passes text_mmap()'s unchecked MAP_FAILED result to strstr(); the optimized libc __strstr_sse2 implementation consequently reads from an invalid address near -1 and aborts, producing the reported denial of service. The same routine also assumed successful mappings were NUL-terminated even though text_mmap() documented only a best-effort terminator, creating a related out-of-bounds scan risk.

**Flaw origin.** Commit a3890282a571bf1754fa20dc325906f05ce70597 upgraded the vendored runtime to AutoGen/libopts 5.18.16 and, for the first time in this repository, added libopts/save.c::remove_settings() plus the update-mode call from open_sv_file(). The new function assigned text_mmap() directly to text/scan and called strstr(scan, zCfgProg) without the failure guard already used by the other text_mmap() callers. Its direct parent 76644c24abde01dcf7f746bb3432b0dcf0b1838a had no remove_settings(), no text_mmap(fname, ...) call, and no strstr(scan, zCfgProg) scan; open_sv_file() instead replaced the file through the older write-mode path. Thus this is new vulnerable behavior rather than a move or refactor of pre-existing vulnerable lines.

**BIC lifecycle.** introducer `a3890282a571bf1754fa20dc325906f05ce70597`; parent `76644c24abde01dcf7f746bb3432b0dcf0b1838a`; parent absence verified `True`; squash decomposed `False`; members `[]`.

**Fix.** fix `b50828c575d0840e5c505f6ab6089d7ab500dea3`; direct fix `abca92c57d4dd24dd2c0768567551d43a09de6dd`.

### 72. GHSA-43w2-q5cj-hwmq — `alias-dc55896ec769693b2520c63e`

- Repository: `classroomio/classroomio`
- Official IDs: `CVE-2025-65669`, `GHSA-43w2-q5cj-hwmq`
- Selection: status `UNANALYZED`; score `161.0`; signals `repo_ai_commit_scan, ai_commits:77, unreviewed_advisory, ghsa_bundle, 2025`.
- Reproduction: bundle `.ai-slop/state/research-queue/round10/case-alias-dc55896ec769693b2520c63e.json`; SHA-256 `05c1a0455306d0a2a9190e8233cf286d83ce590cc79e86d87fdf6ea4dfae47e4`; base revision `1`; raw result `research/round10-top200-20260828/primary/w071.json`.
- Verdict: **NOT_AI**

**Vulnerability semantics.** In the affected ClassroomIO UI, an authenticated student visiting the Explore page receives published courses through the shared Courses/Card component. The card's action-menu guard excludes LMS and landing-page cards but does not exclude isExplore cards, and its Delete action navigates to /courses/{id}/settings#delete. Confirming there calls the browser-side deleteCourse service, which updates the selected course row to status DELETED through Supabase. The v0.1.13 course UPDATE RLS policy delegates to is_user_in_group_with_role(group_id), whose UUID overload accepts any organization member having any non-null role rather than requiring ADMIN/TUTOR, so a student can soft-delete an administrator's published course.

**Flaw origin.** The final causal edge was introduced by 80dc3923461b21699a17157bdfdb050694fca1a5: it replaced the shared course card's non-functional 'WIP: Delete course' alert with a real goto(`/courses/${id}/settings#delete`) action while retaining the menu guard {#if !isLMS && !isOnLandingPage}, which failed to exclude cards rendered by the already-existing student Explore page. Older commits supplied prerequisites rather than the smallest BIC: 98575e4dd9510c60da58e666d27286f8151e9225 (squashed from the PR branch beginning at 3502dedabb9fb3f641a7f510a47435c55f5fd10a) created Explore with the shared card while Delete was still only an alert, and 6ef33cbfd09d01181423861182561692f08ca116 created the browser-side course deletion sink. Commit 80dc3923461b21699a17157bdfdb050694fca1a5 is therefore the smallest commit that first made the disclosed Explore-click path perform deletion.
