### 73. GHSA-gc8m-9gpv-3rpr — `alias-e768c838603f0312734fd037`

- Repository: `appneta/tcpreplay`
- Official IDs: `CVE-2025-9384`, `GHSA-gc8m-9gpv-3rpr`
- Selection: status `UNANALYZED`; score `161.0`; signals `repo_ai_commit_scan, ai_commits:102, unreviewed_advisory, ghsa_bundle, 2025`.
- Reproduction: bundle `.ai-slop/state/research-queue/round10/case-alias-e768c838603f0312734fd037.json`; SHA-256 `a742c34c71c4fd174d77dc1a7551d9ee92b844fcddbac2bade36e9d992dc8f2e`; base revision `1`; raw result `research/round10-top200-20260828/primary/w072.json`.
- Verdict: **NOT_AI**

**Vulnerability semantics.** A local user can make tcprewrite crash during command-line processing with a malformed range such as `--portmap -43:4443`. `tcpedit_post_args` passes the option text to `parse_portmap`, whose `ports2PORT` range branch sees the leading `-`, tokenizes `from_s` on `-`, obtains `from_begin == "43"` but no second token (`from_end == NULL`), and then calls `strtol(from_end, ...)`. The libc conversion dereferences that null pointer before any packet is rewritten, producing the reported SIGSEGV and a local denial of service.

**Flaw origin.** Commit 97a9237005642cf530b0b7d63c906b02460cf4dc introduced the `<port>-<port>:<port>` range feature in `src/tcpedit/portmap.c`. It first added `from_begin = strtok_r(from_s, "-", &token2)`, `from_end = strtok_r(NULL, "-", &token2)`, and unconditional `strtol` calls on both results without validating that either token exists. Later commits moved declarations and adjusted cleanup, but `git log -L` follows the same unguarded second conversion back to 97a9237005642cf530b0b7d63c906b02460cf4dc, making that feature commit the smallest causal introducer rather than a later refactor or merge.

**Vulnerability semantics.** The unauthenticated /reset_password handler generated an absolute password-reset URL with Flask url_for(..., _external=True). Because the application did not configure SERVER_NAME, Flask derived that URL's authority from the request Host header. An attacker could submit a reset request for a victim with an attacker-controlled Host; the emailed link then sent the reset token to the attacker's host when the victim followed it, enabling the attacker to use the token and take over the account.

**Flaw origin.** fb34913357030c170c6e7d6ab64989c6c684fa5d is the smallest causal introducer: it changed the existing reset-request stub in hashview/users/routes.py into a working token-email flow and first added url_for('users.reset_token', token=token, _external=True), while that commit's tree had no SERVER_NAME configuration. The direct parent had only a pass-through send_reset_email stub and contained neither the external reset-link call nor any _external=True occurrence. Later edits guarded unknown users, added user_id, and reformatted the message but preserved the same Host-derived authority mechanism.

**BIC lifecycle.** introducer `fb34913357030c170c6e7d6ab64989c6c684fa5d`; parent `a64d8ea9dd6363ff4dc4303024b3b93a0a9b9c5c`; parent absence verified `True`; squash decomposed `False`; members `[]`.

### 75. GHSA-9v49-c9x8-3hm2 — `alias-f964922f1f24f7c1d96d6163`

- Repository: `appneta/tcpreplay`
- Official IDs: `CVE-2025-9157`, `GHSA-9v49-c9x8-3hm2`
- Selection: status `UNANALYZED`; score `161.0`; signals `repo_ai_commit_scan, ai_commits:102, unreviewed_advisory, ghsa_bundle, 2025`.
- Reproduction: bundle `.ai-slop/state/research-queue/round10/case-alias-f964922f1f24f7c1d96d6163.json`; SHA-256 `95501590d9704cde20e9ff03b7cece37919134fa40c5b8a269ad932193f56b7a`; base revision `1`; raw result `research/round10-top200-20260828/primary/w074.json`.
- Verdict: **NOT_AI**

**Vulnerability semantics.** In tcprewrite's --fixlen pad path, tcpedit_packet derives ip_hdr/ip6_hdr pointers into the packet buffer and then calls untrunc_packet. The added safe_realloc can move the buffer and free the allocation those derived pointers address; execution then continues to rewrite headers and, for IPv4, fix_ipv4_checksums dereferences the stale ip_hdr. A crafted truncated IPv4 capture therefore causes a heap use-after-free (the reporter's AddressSanitizer trace shows the realloc/free in untrunc_packet and the later read in fix_ipv4_checksums).

**Flaw origin.** Commit 69831b8186513309f4dd43ca5bacfc34b554ad14 tried to prevent the existing --fixlen pad out-of-bounds memset by changing untrunc_packet to accept u_char ** and inserting packet = safe_realloc(packet, pkthdr->len), but it neither rebased the already-derived IP header pointers nor, in that commit's tree, assigned the moved packet back through *pktdata before returning. This is the first commit to introduce a realloc/free between header derivation and subsequent header/checksum use. The later 64132c54c4000046b30f1fc3fe612db9b2f26860 only increased that already-vulnerable allocation by PACKET_HEADROOM and is not the BIC.

**BIC lifecycle.** introducer `69831b8186513309f4dd43ca5bacfc34b554ad14`; parent `16abc7fe749bd3c130204d0b2707caf7cab5894e`; parent absence verified `True`; squash decomposed `False`; members `[]`.

**AI marker on BIC.** absent — the raw commit object for 69831b8186513309f4dd43ca5bacfc34b554ad14 has author Fred Klassen <fklassen@appneta.com>, committer Fred Klassen <fklassen@appneta.com>, and only the message 'remalloc packets before padding to ensure not overwriting memory - closes #80'; it has no Co-Authored-By, Generated-with, AI-assistant trailer, or bot identity.

**Fix.** fix `73008f261f1cdf7a1087dc8759115242696d35da`; direct fix `73008f261f1cdf7a1087dc8759115242696d35da`.

**Reviewer-ready evidence.**

- First-party disclosure: https://github.com/appneta/tcpreplay/issues/970 identifies src/tcpedit/edit_packet.c, reports the --fixlen pad reproducer, and gives an AddressSanitizer allocation/free stack in untrunc_packet followed by the stale IPv4-header read in fix_ipv4_checksums; https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-9v49-c9x8-3hm2 identifies CVE-2025-9157 and affected versions through 4.5.2-beta2. Origin search: `git log --all --full-history --reverse -S'packet = safe_realloc(packet, pkthdr->len);' -- src/tcpedit/edit_packet.c` returns 69831b8186513309f4dd43ca5bacfc34b554ad14 as the addition and 64132c54c4000046b30f1fc3fe612db9b2f26860 as the later size-expression replacement; a separate pickaxe for the PACKET_HEADROOM expression returns only 64132c54c4000046b30f1fc3fe612db9b2f26860 and its removal by the fix. BIC source: 69831b8186513309f4dd43ca5bacfc34b554ad14 adds `packet = safe_realloc(packet, pkthdr->len)` at src/tcpedit/edit_packet.c:275 after header pointers have been derived; src/common/utils.c:67-77 shows safe_realloc calls libc realloc. In the same tree src/tcpedit/tcpedit.c:225-228 calls untrunc_packet with the derived ip_hdr/ip6_hdr and lines 231-293 subsequently reuse those pointers, including fix_ipv4_checksums at line 290. Direct-parent proof: `git show 16abc7fe749bd3c130204d0b2707caf7cab5894e:src/tcpedit/edit_packet.c` shows the pad branch directly calling memset on pktdata and contains no safe_realloc, while the BIC diff replaces that line with the realloc plus memset and changes the API/caller; thus the realloc-driven UAF lines are absent from the one direct parent (although that parent had the distinct overwrite bug the BIC intended to repair). The BIC is an ordinary one-parent commit, not a merge/squash aggregate. Version boundaries: v4.0.4 does not contain the BIC; `git for-each-ref --contains=69831b... refs/tags` begins at v4.0.5beta1 (d0676bfe5f2bddc73a60e9a01a89eeeb2de01eab). v4.5.2-beta2 resolves to 61dd7853b54baa436fbd458e8bfd93d2bdbb00a9, contains the BIC, and does not contain the fix (`git merge-base --is-ancestor` exits 1 for fix -> v4.5.2-beta2). Fix evidence: https://github.com/appneta/tcpreplay/commit/73008f261f1cdf7a1087dc8759115242696d35da is direct commit 73008f261f1cdf7a1087dc8759115242696d35da (parent a1778a25a2f8dc4de879782567abab6b923e9694); it removes safe_realloc from src/tcpedit/edit_packet.c:574-576, adds a pkthdr.len > MAX_SNAPLEN guard in src/tcprewrite.c, bumps configure.ac from 4.5.2-beta2 to 4.5.2-beta3, and records #970 in docs/CHANGELOG. `git tag --contains 73008f...` starts at v4.5.2; that tag resolves to 98169912173986cc48a4ad325997dcc20c38af28 and contains the fix, matching the advisory's last-affected 4.5.2-beta2 boundary. AI check: `git cat-file -p 69831b8186513309f4dd43ca5bacfc34b554ad14` yields the exact human author/committer and trailer-free message quoted in ai_marker.

**Reasoning.** The first-party report establishes the vulnerable data flow: a truncated IPv4 packet reaches untrunc_packet through --fixlen pad, realloc may free/move the packet, and checksum calculation later reads a header pointer into the freed allocation. History then distinguishes the true origin from a tempting 2020 blame result: 64132c54c4000046b30f1fc3fe612db9b2f26860 merely changed the reallocation size, whereas 69831b8186513309f4dd43ca5bacfc34b554ad14 first inserted any realloc into this path. Its direct parent 16abc7fe749bd3c130204d0b2707caf7cab5894e has no realloc, so this specific UAF mechanism is parent-absent. The BIC predates the first containing tag v4.0.5beta1 and remains in the advisory's last vulnerable tag v4.5.2-beta2. Fix 73008f261f1cdf7a1087dc8759115242696d35da removes the unnecessary realloc and bounds declared length to the already-allocated packet capacity; it is absent from v4.5.2-beta2 and present in v4.5.2. Finally, attribution is based only on the BIC's raw commit object: it identifies Fred Klassen as both author and committer and contains no AI/bot marker, so the closed causal verdict is NOT_AI.

### 76. GHSA-5qwm-7pvp-w988 — `alias-636f2d15846304fa7f039c27`

- Repository: `openmcdf/openmcdf`
- Official IDs: `CVE-2026-45785`, `GHSA-5qwm-7pvp-w988`
- Selection: status `UNANALYZED`; score `160.925`; signals `repo_ai_commit_scan, ai_commits:11, reviewed_advisory, ghsa_bundle, 2026`.
- Reproduction: bundle `.ai-slop/state/research-queue/round10/case-alias-636f2d15846304fa7f039c27.json`; SHA-256 `09fbf1df27b3897c1726ede9902ff6c137185519e49e24df95a64f2b85f01be9`; base revision `1`; raw result `research/round10-top200-20260828/primary/w075.json`.
- Verdict: **NOT_AI**

**Vulnerability semantics.** A crafted CFB directory can make the child-directed binary-search path cycle through LeftSiblingId/RightSiblingId entries. DirectoryTree.TryGetDirectoryEntry repeatedly compares the requested name and follows one sibling while child is non-null; the pre-fix TryGetSibling check validates only the current parent/sibling ordering, so a multi-node cycle can satisfy every local comparison and never reach a match or NoStream. RootStorage.OpenStorage/TryOpenStorage/OpenStream/TryOpenStream all reach this lookup, leaving the affected thread in an uncatchable CPU-consuming loop.

**Flaw origin.** Commit 92cc9d74b7c4a63cf78625fbeaa5fa9207a01344 introduced OpenMcdf3/DirectoryTree.cs and, specifically, the new direct BST name-lookup implementation: while child is non-null it compares the target with child.NameCharSpan and replaces child with the selected LeftSiblingId or RightSiblingId entry, with no visited-node, step-bound, or whole-search-order state. This was not merely a path move: its direct parent used DirectoryTreeEnumerator.MoveTo for lookup and had no DirectoryTree.cs or child-directed BST lookup loop; 92cc9d74 newly wrote the mechanism fixed by the advisory patch.

**BIC lifecycle.** introducer `92cc9d74b7c4a63cf78625fbeaa5fa9207a01344`; parent `cb9cb9d7cb0d5fa8e12577631f106dd810fb1966`; parent absence verified `True`; squash decomposed `False`; members `[]`.

**AI marker on BIC.** absent: the exact commit object for 92cc9d74b7c4a63cf78625fbeaa5fa9207a01344 has author Jeremy Powell <jeremy@visionaid.com>, committer Jeremy Powell <jeremy@visionaid.com>, subject 'Add initial DirectoryTree implementation', and no message body or Co-Authored-By, Generated-with, bot, or other AI marker.

**Fix.** fix `c6f82db722bd85db7b0caed3ca1aa374f1e07bc7`; direct fix `c6f82db722bd85db7b0caed3ca1aa374f1e07bc7`.

**Reviewer-ready evidence.**

- First-party advisory https://github.com/openmcdf/openmcdf/security/advisories/GHSA-5qwm-7pvp-w988 identifies CVE-2026-45785/GHSA-5qwm-7pvp-w988, OpenMcdf/DirectoryTree.cs:35-46 and DirectoryEntries.cs:84-85, the OpenStorage/TryOpenStorage/OpenStream/TryOpenStream attack paths, affected versions <=3.1.3, and patched version 3.1.4. `git log -L 26,51:OpenMcdf/DirectoryTree.cs` traces the child-directed TryGetDirectoryEntry loop to 92cc9d74b7c4a63cf78625fbeaa5fa9207a01344; that commit's first-party page is https://github.com/openmcdf/openmcdf/commit/92cc9d74b7c4a63cf78625fbeaa5fa9207a01344 and its patch adds OpenMcdf3/DirectoryTree.cs lines 23-52 containing the unbounded loop. `git ls-tree -r --name-only cb9cb9d7cb0d5fa8e12577631f106dd810fb1966 -- OpenMcdf3/DirectoryTree.cs` returns no path, and direct inspection of cb9cb9d7cb0d5fa8e12577631f106dd810fb1966:OpenMcdf3/DirectoryTreeEnumerator.cs shows lookup instead went through MoveTo/MoveNext, proving the advisory's direct child-selected BST loop absent from the immediate parent. `git cat-file commit 92cc9d74b7c4a63cf78625fbeaa5fa9207a01344` proves the one-parent commit object and the exact human author/committer/message with no AI trailer. The direct first-party fix https://github.com/openmcdf/openmcdf/commit/c6f82db722bd85db7b0caed3ca1aa374f1e07bc7 says 'Fixes: GHSA-5qwm-7pvp-w988'; it adds OpenMcdf/DirectoryTreeSearchOrderValidator.cs, carries min/max bounds across each search, and changes OpenMcdf/DirectoryTree.cs plus OpenMcdf/DirectoryEntries.cs so every selected sibling is checked against the accumulated global bounds, causing a cyclic path to throw FileFormatException instead of repeating. Its RootStorageTests.cs regression opens DirectoryTreeCycle.cfb and expects FileFormatException from TryOpenStorage. ### 77. GHSA-43h9-hc38-qph5 — `alias-6aa79fbe1dfdb464d0d1630c`

- Verdict: **NOT_AI**

**Vulnerability semantics.** SQLE used the public constant string "secret" as the HMAC key both to sign JWTs and to authenticate JWTs protecting the /v1 API. Because HS256 verification proves only knowledge of that shared key, a remote attacker who knows the repository-visible constant can create a syntactically valid token with attacker-chosen claims, including an administrative name, and have the middleware accept it. The same default later survived as JWTSecretKey = []byte("secret") in sqle/utils/jwt.go; although a setter was added, current history has no SetSecretKey callsite, so the default remains effective.

**Flaw origin.** Commit 70dd2812fff6ffa3e60cd5cdc550c3f6979a83a0 first added JWT authentication and, in the same change, created sqle/api/controller/auth_v1.go with const JWTSecret = "secret", signed login tokens with that value at line 39, and configured sqle/api/app.go:82 to verify /v1 tokens with the same value. Later commits ee756efd4a6d393edf918292584001ff9706f4bb and e0604a3eb459e6e1260610a5bf937fd0d34cef22 only moved/refactored the already-vulnerable constant, while d81fd4a1aabff13765f8db9060758bd9f11dc3c7 rewrote it as the still-hard-coded []byte variable; none is the BIC.

**BIC lifecycle.** introducer `70dd2812fff6ffa3e60cd5cdc550c3f6979a83a0`; parent `70757e49453c461398cf61515a94fd116b8a96d7`; parent absence verified `True`; squash decomposed `False`; members `[]`.

Its direct parent had no user-management routes at all. The PR was later squash-landed as 1133202cbd12ec6a92fa1b446889ff2d75986def; the later viewer-role work in 74ca009b0b767a8393562a932673f8fd5b11b7fe made the latent missing per-action authorization exploitable by a formally low-privilege role but did not originate the delete handler.

Parent Storage walked directory sectors and would terminate; the new stack walk never tracks visited IDs. DirectoryTree.TryGetDirectoryEntry (92cc9d74b7c4a63cf78625fbeaa5fa9207a01344) later added a second unguarded BST sibling walk used by OpenStream; that is a follow-on rewrite of the same missing cycle check, not the first write.

BIC b2fc989e4c3e6b682c8416bf5aa72b3fe37ae9e3 (single parent 7821a5d148cb523d1f3c347680c5eeccc25de3e3) adds OpenMcdf3/DirectoryTreeEnumerator.cs whose PushLeft follows LeftSiblingID and MoveNext follows RightSiblingID with no visited set; Storage.EnumerateDirectoryEntries and OpenStream both used that enumerator. git cat-file -e 7821a5d148cb523d1f3c347680c5eeccc25de3e3:OpenMcdf3/DirectoryTreeEnumerator.cs fails; parent Storage.cs enumerates FAT directory sectors linearly. git cat-file -p on the BIC shows author/committer Jeremy Powell <jeremy@visionaid.com> with subject Allow storage directory entry enumeration and no Co-Authored-By / Generated-with / bot author. Later 92cc9d74b7c4a63cf78625fbeaa5fa9207a01344 first adds DirectoryTree.TryGetDirectoryEntry (unguarded sibling walk) but rewrites rather than first-introduces the cycle-vulnerable traversal.

Because the required closed verdict cannot substitute a later migration snapshot or rewrite for the smallest BIC, the correct result is BLOCKED at the VCS-history boundary rather than NOT_AI.

**Remaining gap.** Re-adjudicated: none — see reasoning prefix. Original gap: The precise unreachable fact is a full lowercase 40-hex Git commit ID (and 40-hex Git parent) for the true BIC, SourceForge SVN r4. ### 81. GHSA-xm8c-hvjf-c5q9 — `alias-bac68e1dd4afde4efda680e9`

- Repository: `raineorshine/npm-check-updates`
- Official IDs: `CVE-2026-73035`, `GHSA-xm8c-hvjf-c5q9`
- Selection: status `UNANALYZED`; score `160.534`; signals `repo_ai_commit_scan, ai_commits:29, unreviewed_advisory, ghsa_bundle, 2026`.
- Reproduction: bundle `.ai-slop/state/research-queue/round10/case-alias-bac68e1dd4afde4efda680e9.json`; SHA-256 `f151826d7ecf64a32fae497d1ce51c2659eb26a18066ba9fac72eb82eec04cbc`; base revision `1`; raw result `research/round10-top200-20260828/primary/w080.json`.
- Verdict: **NOT_AI**

**Vulnerability semantics.** A dependency controls its installed package.json repository and homepage fields. When a user requests repository/homepage columns, npm-check-updates places those strings into a cli-table3 row and prints the row without neutralizing ESC, OSC, CSI, CR, or other terminal control characters. A malicious dependency value therefore reaches the user's terminal and can manipulate terminal-rendered output when ncu is run with the relevant format option.

**Flaw origin.** Commit 43bac8b12f6cdbc121c11cc0839e97d7abba0138 first created the vulnerable repository-display path. In lib/logging.js lines 89-92 it computed repoUrl as getRepoUrl(dep) || '' and appended it directly to the terminal table row; the same commit's new lib/repo-url.js returned a qualifying packageJson.repository string verbatim. Commit c273d79d7ea5daa2cdf9000120c8f5e7f084017b later extended the same unsanitized table mechanism to packageJson.homepage. Refactors and option renames preserved the original repository sink until the fix.

**BIC lifecycle.** introducer `43bac8b12f6cdbc121c11cc0839e97d7abba0138`; parent `2ae1ed2d0573d086815dfb7d98e7ecc82aeb0a11`; parent absence verified `True`; squash decomposed `False`; members `[]`.

**AI marker on BIC.** absent: the exact commit object for 43bac8b12f6cdbc121c11cc0839e97d7abba0138 names author Jason O'Neill <CreativeTechGuy@users.noreply.github.com> and committer Jason O'Neill <CreativeTechGuy@users.noreply.github.com>; its message is only 'Add repo urls to new --output command', with no Co-Authored-By, Generated-with, AI-tool trailer, or bot identity.

**Fix.** fix `b554b84848fc0b08a9d2b3d3db15e351387168cf`; direct fix `b554b84848fc0b08a9d2b3d3db15e351387168cf`.

**Reviewer-ready evidence.**

- First-party advisory https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-xm8c-hvjf-c5q9 (GHSA-xm8c-hvjf-c5q9 / CVE-2026-73035) describes unfiltered terminal-control characters from dependency package.json homepage or repository URL fields reaching ncu --format homepage/repo output through 23.0.2 and identifies b554b84848fc0b08a9d2b3d3db15e351387168cf as the fix; the advisory's structured affected and patched version fields are themselves Unknown.
- First-party report https://github.com/raineorshine/npm-check-updates/issues/1988 identifies src/lib/logging.ts as the output path and records an offline reproduction in which an OSC title-setting sequence from a dependency homepage appeared unmodified in captured stdout. First-party fix PR https://github.com/raineorshine/npm-check-updates/pull/1994 says it fixes #1988.
- numactl-prefixed git log -L over the homepageUrl/repoUrl block and reverse git log -S 'getRepoUrl(dep)' across lib/logging.js, src/logging.js, src/logging.ts, and src/lib/logging.ts trace the earliest repository sink to 43bac8b12f6cdbc121c11cc0839e97d7abba0138. The -L history distinguishes later changes: c273d79d7ea5daa2cdf9000120c8f5e7f084017b added the homepage branch; a427316534f637f13edbb7b8259557d0d694d6e6 only renamed repositoryLink to repo; subsequent moves/refactors retained the sink.
- The BIC diff at https://github.com/raineorshine/npm-check-updates/commit/43bac8b12f6cdbc121c11cc0839e97d7abba0138 adds lib/logging.js lines 89-92, where getRepoUrl(dep) is appended to the table row without sanitization, and adds lib/repo-url.js, whose direct-HTTPS branch returns the original gitURL string. git blame at the BIC attributes all four sink lines to 43bac8b12f6cdbc121c11cc0839e97d7abba0138.
- Direct-parent verification used the BIC object's sole parent 2ae1ed2d0573d086815dfb7d98e7ecc82aeb0a11 and a parent-tree git grep for repositoryLink|getRepoUrl|repoUrl under lib; it returned no matches. The BIC diff also shows lib/repo-url.js as a new file and the raw repoUrl table cells as additions, proving the vulnerable path is absent from the immediate parent.
- Version-boundary checks show the BIC parent describes from v10.0.0, while the version-sorted tags containing the BIC begin at v10.1.0 and v10.1.0's package.json declares 10.1.0. The BIC is an ancestor of advisory-listed last-vulnerable tag v23.0.2. The fix is not an ancestor of v23.0.2, is an ancestor of v23.1.0, and the version-sorted tags containing it begin at v23.1.0; package.json at those tags declares 23.0.2 and 23.1.0 respectively.
- The first-party fix commit https://github.com/raineorshine/npm-check-updates/commit/b554b84848fc0b08a9d2b3d3db15e351387168cf changes src/lib/logging.ts so both packageJson.homepage and getRepoUrl(...) pass through sanitizeForDisplay before entering the table. sanitizeForDisplay applies node:util stripVTControlCharacters and then removes remaining C0/C1 controls, including bare CR. The commit adds regression coverage for OSC in homepage and CR in repository data.

**Reasoning.** The vulnerability is a source-to-sink failure: attacker-influenced metadata in an installed dependency's package.json is selected for an optional display column and then printed by the terminal table without control-sequence neutralization. History establishes two entry points into one flawed mechanism. The repository route is older: 43bac8b12f6cdbc121c11cc0839e97d7abba0138 both introduced getRepoUrl and directly inserted its result into the displayed row, so it is the smallest causal BIC rather than later renames, TypeScript moves, inline refactors, or the 2026 homepage expansion. Its sole direct parent's tree contains none of the repository-display symbols, and the introduced source file/table lines are additions. No squash decomposition is needed because this one-parent member commit itself contains the causal code rather than merely moving or aggregating an earlier implementation. The BIC entered release v10.1.0 and remained ancestral to v23.0.2. Commit b554b84848fc0b08a9d2b3d3db15e351387168cf directly closes both homepage and repository paths by sanitizing immediately before display and is first present in v23.1.0. Finally, the exact BIC commit object has a human author/committer and no AI marker, so BIC-only attribution requires NOT_AI regardless of later commits or the fix authorship.

### 82. GHSA-r8rp-5f55-5j9x — `alias-26a1c524547a0de4144d510f`

- Verdict: **NOT_AI**

**Vulnerability semantics.** The authenticated PUT /admin/settings/users/edit/{id} route accepts an attacker-controlled user id, and UserController::update validates request fields but performs no object-level authorization tying that id to the acting user before passing attacker-controlled data to UserRepository::update. A low-privilege account with the users.edit ACL permission can therefore target another user's id, submit a new password (which is bcrypt-hashed), and take over or deactivate that account.

**Flaw origin.** The unsafe update sink already existed as unreachable controller code, but fc536cbc35cbd3e095379ae0934784b12f6b033e is the smallest causal introducer: it first registered Route::put('edit/{id}', 'UserController@update') beneath only the authenticated user middleware, making the attacker-controlled id reach the authorization-free password-update handler. Its direct parent still had UserController::update but no update route, so the reported HTTP attack path was absent.

**BIC lifecycle.** introducer `fc536cbc35cbd3e095379ae0934784b12f6b033e`; parent `c155fb4d8f3d94bcddb2a46d8e691f326220fb79`; parent absence verified `True`; squash decomposed `False`; members `[]`.

### 83. GHSA-j822-46r5-h4qx — `alias-2adf0bc290aee74c6b9a8b3a`

- Repository: `krayin/laravel-crm`
- Official IDs: `CVE-2026-36341`, `GHSA-j822-46r5-h4qx`
- Selection: status `UNANALYZED`; score `160.297`; signals `repo_ai_commit_scan, ai_commits:10, reviewed_advisory, ghsa_bundle, 2026`.

- Verdict: **FALSE_POSITIVE**

**Vulnerability semantics.** An authenticated low-privilege CRM user can POST an attacker-controlled comment to the admin activities create route. ActivityController validates presence but passes request()->all() into ActivityRepository without neutralizing comment, ActivityResource returns the stored comment unchanged, and the shared activities component interprets it as HTML when another user views the activity. That stored-data-to-HTML-sink chain permits persistent attacker-controlled markup and, as reported by GHSA-j822-46r5-h4qx and upstream issue #2419, stored XSS across users including administrators.

**Flaw origin.** Commit fabc2c41978bad04d16b0a9098dd6288e68e3a06 made the first unsafe output-boundary transition in packages/Webkul/Admin/src/Resources/views/components/activities/index.blade.php: it replaced Vue's escaped @{{ activity.comment }} interpolation with v-html="activity.comment" while the create/update and JSON-resource paths continued carrying the comment verbatim. Commit 4848b68af8ce1b973fc60018860c8a8347d2b7bd later changed v-html to a DOMPurify-backed v-safe-html directive, reducing some script vectors but retaining HTML interpretation; the definitive fix restored escaped text interpolation.

**BIC lifecycle.** introducer —; parent —; parent absence verified `True`; squash decomposed `False`; members `[]`.

### 84. GHSA-32px-ccfx-cxq3 — `alias-63576fe0837a37b72bc927f1`

- Repository: `krayin/laravel-crm`
- Official IDs: `CVE-2026-36340`, `GHSA-32px-ccfx-cxq3`
- Selection: status `UNANALYZED`; score `160.297`; signals `repo_ai_commit_scan, ai_commits:10, reviewed_advisory, ghsa_bundle, 2026`.
- Reproduction: bundle `.ai-slop/state/research-queue/round10/case-alias-63576fe0837a37b72bc927f1.json`; SHA-256 `5ac5413f149702b4b8cdcbbbdb1ba383480a12c4fc58b5a473847567bff4e199`; base revision `1`; raw result `research/round10-top200-20260828/primary/w083.json`.
- Verdict: **NOT_AI**

**Vulnerability semantics.** An authenticated user can submit a PHP attachment to POST /admin/mail/create. The email attachment repository preserves the client-controlled filename, including an executable extension, and writes the bytes through the default public filesystem disk beneath storage/app/public/emails/<email-id>/; the configured public/storage symlink exposes that file at /storage/emails/<email-id>/<filename>, where a PHP-capable web server executes it.

**Flaw origin.** Commit c42bad26269130aed2ef25ae4959b956fc754485 refactored web and inbound attachment handling into prepareData() and, for web UploadedFile objects, replaced Laravel's directory-only UploadedFile::store('emails/<id>') call with a path assembled from getClientOriginalName() followed by Storage::put(). That semantic change first made the attacker-supplied compose-upload filename part of the public on-disk path; it was not a mere move of already-vulnerable compose logic.

**BIC lifecycle.** introducer `c42bad26269130aed2ef25ae4959b956fc754485`; parent `56ee80d9d85afd8bffff652df872d7c96d9ab748`; parent absence verified `True`; squash decomposed `False`; members `[]`.

**AI marker on BIC.** absent: numactl --cpunodebind=1 --membind=1 git cat-file -p c42bad26269130aed2ef25ae4959b956fc754485 shows author and committer Suraj Kashyap <suraj.kashyap370@webkul.in> and message 'fix: resolve attachment display issue and TinyMCE editor visibility'; the BIC commit object has no Co-Authored-By trailer, Generated-with trailer, bot identity, or other AI-authorship marker.

**Fix.** fix `ea4919a8e362bd817d0b879527194189f7f7c889`; direct fix `4d818957bd5e32abef89d4708438f55a007fa8b5`.

**Reviewer-ready evidence.**

### 85. GHSA-fpx9-9hq8-w2xc — `alias-6f1cbee9eb7ea1bbbb8280a1`

- Repository: `krayin/laravel-crm`
- Official IDs: `CVE-2026-38527`, `GHSA-fpx9-9hq8-w2xc`
- Selection: status `UNANALYZED`; score `160.297`; signals `repo_ai_commit_scan, ai_commits:10, reviewed_advisory, ghsa_bundle, 2026`.
- Reproduction: bundle `.ai-slop/state/research-queue/round10/case-alias-6f1cbee9eb7ea1bbbb8280a1.json`; SHA-256 `5e43d46008930eec398a5c78af3e9c0b85b1a051f2d079e79904df797655885d`; base revision `1`; raw result `research/round10-top200-20260828/primary/w084.json`.
- Verdict: **NOT_AI**

**Vulnerability semantics.** A user who can configure CRM workflows/webhooks can supply an attacker-chosen destination URL. The application stores that URL and, when the workflow fires, sends an HTTP request from the CRM server without first constraining the scheme or rejecting loopback, private, link-local, reserved, or cloud-metadata destinations. This lets the user reach otherwise inaccessible internal services and infer or receive their responses. In the advisory's current route, POST /admin/settings/webhooks/create accepts end_point and the workflow dispatcher passes it to Guzzle.

**Flaw origin.** The underlying SSRF mechanism first became executable in ea3f9d66dbea8f56a5edbf3ab09323ae12c6e52e: packages/Webkul/Workflow/src/Helpers/Entity/Lead.php began passing the workflow-controlled action['hook']['url'] directly to Http::withHeaders(...)->post(...) without destination validation. The direct parent already had the webhook URL form but no outbound webhook request sink, so ea3f9d66dbea8f56a5edbf3ab09323ae12c6e52e is the smallest commit that completed the flaw. Later commits extended the same behavior to more entities, renamed Workflow to Automation, and centralized dispatch. In particular, 9bebb377ed610c10658092de580f2614aa6793db created the /settings/webhooks/create storage path with end_point validated only as required|string|max:255, and dec043c2d10241d2ea5051019595e9633b251b51 connected stored endpoints to a new unguarded Guzzle WebhookService; those are feature evolution/refactoring of the already-existing unvalidated webhook-request mechanism, not the original BIC.

**BIC lifecycle.** introducer `dec043c2d10241d2ea5051019595e9633b251b51`; parent `245c4b1ba1317d6043cad315d431aa58c63e1264`; parent absence verified `False`; squash decomposed `False`; members `[]`.

**AI marker on BIC.** absent — the exact BIC commit object names both author and committer as prabhat gautam <prabhatkumar.oc082@webkul.in>; its message is "some more changes in UI and added sent post request" and has no Co-Authored-By, Generated-with, AI-tool, or bot marker/trailer.

**Fix.** fix `556dda0471880fc931da6f4d38ddbc949a458eec`; direct fix `7f6b82de87ed64ba4ab5edc1b186006689a6ae92`.

**Reviewer-ready evidence.**

### 86. GHSA-rm5f-3c25-p4cw — `alias-7e9f8c189a08a1febf266038`

- Repository: `krayin/laravel-crm`
- Official IDs: `CVE-2026-38530`, `GHSA-rm5f-3c25-p4cw`
- Selection: status `UNANALYZED`; score `160.297`; signals `repo_ai_commit_scan, ai_commits:10, reviewed_advisory, ghsa_bundle, 2026`.
- Reproduction: bundle `.ai-slop/state/research-queue/round10/case-alias-7e9f8c189a08a1febf266038.json`; SHA-256 `8a03234d712f8c0935cc78269d08290b6b50cc9c429870a8aa0133ce3006280d`; base revision `1`; raw result `research/round10-top200-20260828/primary/w085.json`.
- Verdict: **NOT_AI**

**Vulnerability semantics.** Authenticated CRM users with route-level lead permissions could supply another user's lead ID to direct LeadController endpoints. The controller fetched or mutated that ID without checking the lead's user_id against bouncer()->getAuthorizedUserIds(); list and view-permission scoping therefore did not protect the direct edit/update/delete paths, enabling cross-user disclosure, modification, reassignment, and deletion.

**Flaw origin.** Commit bd24ddb6ebcf4a2d527d71ecb3a4f5d3fea85399 first made the enduring destructive form of the flaw executable: it simultaneously added DELETE leads/{id} -> LeadController@destroy in packages/Webkul/Admin/src/Http/routes.php and added LeadController::destroy() in packages/Webkul/Admin/src/Http/Controllers/Lead/LeadController.php. The new method accepted the caller-controlled ID, checked only that the row existed, and then called $this->leadRepository->delete($id), with no ownership or authorized-user comparison.

**BIC lifecycle.** introducer `bd24ddb6ebcf4a2d527d71ecb3a4f5d3fea85399`; parent `85cf437139289e0cd305c1cfde35d5d3028f556c`; parent absence verified `True`; squash decomposed `False`; members `[]`.

**AI marker on BIC.** absent: the exact BIC commit object names author Shubham Mehrotra <shubh0896m@gmail.com> and the identical human committer, contains only the subject 'design fixes, lead creation, user account', has no Co-Authored-By or Generated-with trailer, no bot identity, and no other AI-attribution marker.

**Fix.** fix `e1eb78586fc1bba0204de12222a7f10b53986cc9`; direct fix `cccc12df2c405f6c00633bff13d7befd8dd0ee4f`.

**Reviewer-ready evidence.**

- Advisory sources: https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-rm5f-3c25-p4cw and https://github.com/TREXNEGRO/Security-Advisories/tree/main/CVE-2026-38530 describe the missing owner check in packages/Webkul/Admin/src/Http/Controllers/Lead/LeadController.php and the crafted GET/PUT/DELETE lead-ID attack. First-party repository issue https://github.com/krayin/laravel-crm/issues/2559 independently documents that route ACL middleware does not enforce record ownership, reproduces cross-user edit/updateAttributes/delete, and identifies the same controller; https://github.com/krayin/laravel-crm/issues/2462 records the same systemic IDOR. History proof: git log -L over LeadController::destroy and git log -S'$this->leadRepository->delete($id)' both trace the surviving deletion line to https://github.com/krayin/laravel-crm/commit/bd24ddb6ebcf4a2d527d71ecb3a4f5d3fea85399. That BIC's diff adds both packages/Webkul/Admin/src/Http/routes.php DELETE '{id}' -> LeadController@destroy and packages/Webkul/Admin/src/Http/Controllers/Lead/LeadController.php destroy(), whose findOrFail($id) is followed by delete($id) without owner authorization. Direct-parent tree checks at 85cf437139289e0cd305c1cfde35d5d3028f556c find neither the destroy method/deletion line nor the DELETE route, proving absence. The BIC is contained by the first release tag v1.0.0 and every later tag. Boundary checks show the unguarded find/delete lines and no preventUnauthorizedAccess call in v2.2.0 (a282e7c3cf969bf10ccc8ebd636be502a58a5a9b), v2.2.1 (a651f7f3a029f16ccbb2e6461f4c4f64badfb04e), v2.2.2 (e0670bb8f0c0bb72aab430d070eb86bd8114ff71), and v2.2.3 (6cda4f6297042d74769c38fcbc1b7ebe6df54ab6); thus the advisory's published '<= 2.2.0' range understates the source-visible affected boundary. Direct fix https://github.com/krayin/laravel-crm/commit/cccc12df2c405f6c00633bff13d7befd8dd0ee4f adds Controller::preventUnauthorizedAccess()/filterAuthorizedRecords() and applies the ownership check before LeadController edit, update, updateAttributes, updateStage, destroy, massUpdate, and massDestroy. First-party PR https://github.com/krayin/laravel-crm/pull/2567 lands that direct fix through merge https://github.com/krayin/laravel-crm/commit/e1eb78586fc1bba0204de12222a7f10b53986cc9. Both the merge and direct fix are contained by v2.2.4 (55b48fe86d7f196c32581ed80bb723cf0e18d44e), whose controller contains the guards, making v2.2.4 the first source-proven patched tag; the advisory itself supplies no first_patched_version.

**Reasoning.** The causal unit is not a later refactor or the broad 2026 fix: bd24ddb6ebcf4a2d527d71ecb3a4f5d3fea85399 is the smallest ordinary one-parent commit that first wired an attacker-reachable lead deletion endpoint and wrote its unscoped repository deletion. Its direct parent lacks both route and method, while git -L/-S show the deletion survived subsequent formatting/refactors into the advisory-tested 2.2.x code. Later ownership-aware listing/view logic made the authorization asymmetry explicit, but did not originate the enduring deletion line. The flaw remained in tagged releases through v2.2.3. Direct commit cccc12df2c405f6c00633bff13d7befd8dd0ee4f fixes the mechanism by checking the record owner against the authorized-user set before direct operations, and merge e1eb78586fc1bba0204de12222a7f10b53986cc9 lands PR #2567 before v2.2.4. AI attribution is judged only from the BIC object; its human author/committer and trailer-free message contain no AI marker, so the closed verdict is NOT_AI.

### 87. GHSA-2vwp-xrw2-3m34 — `alias-b84638a5232179ddf43e6003`

- Repository: `zackees/transcribe-anything`
- Official IDs: `CVE-2026-79792`, `GHSA-2vwp-xrw2-3m34`
- Selection: status `UNANALYZED`; score `160.29`; signals `repo_ai_commit_scan, ai_commits:28, unreviewed_advisory, ghsa_bundle, 2026`.
- Reproduction: bundle `.ai-slop/state/research-queue/round10/case-alias-b84638a5232179ddf43e6003.json`; SHA-256 `65c4dda1a1a2aa22feb3f4cc8d987c4aa9f41813914bd03e5ddc0a6669d793a9`; base revision `1`; raw result `research/round10-top200-20260828/primary/w086.json`.
- Verdict: **NOT_AI**

**Vulnerability semantics.** An attacker-influenced URL reaches transcribe_anything.api.transcribe(url_or_file), which passes it to audio.fetch_audio after only a startswith("http")/startswith("ftp") routing check. fetch_audio calls ytdlp_download, where src/transcribe_anything/ytldp_download.py interpolates url without quoting or validation into a single yt-dlp command string and executes that string with subprocess.run(..., shell=True). Shell metacharacters in the URL are therefore parsed as commands and run with the transcribing process's privileges (CWE-78/CWE-77 command injection); the project has no default listener, so remote exploitation requires an integration that forwards attacker-controlled URLs.

**Flaw origin.** The smallest origin is 7247b8c3fbdcdb625ab42389b2cc0781383e5e1c, which first added transcribe_anything/run.py and, in fetch_mono_16000_audio, placed url_or_file unquoted in an f-string youtube-dl command and immediately ran cmd with shell=True. Later commits changed youtube-dl to yt-dlp, reshaped the helper, extracted it to transcribe_anything/ytldp_download.py, and moved the package under src/; those are evolutionary edits/moves, not the origin of the flawed URL-to-shell mechanism.

**BIC lifecycle.** introducer `7247b8c3fbdcdb625ab42389b2cc0781383e5e1c`; parent `a7aa39feed35b757edf9ca1fc79f99f6296ced2f`; parent absence verified `True`; squash decomposed `False`; members `[]`.

### 88. GHSA-rm43-82j9-r4mj — `alias-46e86e6eec01a23b67b79120`

- Repository: `dep0we/atomic-agents-stack`
- Official IDs: `GHSA-rm43-82j9-r4mj`
- Selection: status `UNANALYZED`; score `160.0`; signals `repo_ai_commit_scan, ai_commits:273, reviewed_advisory, ghsa_bundle`.
- Reproduction: bundle `.ai-slop/state/research-queue/round10/case-alias-46e86e6eec01a23b67b79120.json`; SHA-256 `a55021164dc6afc0d9d22592125ca379a31e45d7192c7f135bb02b81801f808d`; base revision `1`; raw result `research/round10-top200-20260828/primary/w087.json`.
- Verdict: **NOT_AI**

**Vulnerability semantics.** atomic_agents/dashboard/serve.py DashboardHandler.do_GET takes urlparse(self.path).path and joins it into filesystem paths with no containment check, then _serve_file reads whatever exists. Three untrusted-path branches first appear together: GET /agents/<name> does agents_root / agent_name / dashboard.html; GET /_dashboard/<rel> does agents_root / path.lstrip('/'); a bare filename does agents_root / '_dashboard' / path.lstrip('/'). Literal '../' segments survive urlparse and pathlib joining, so requests such as GET /../../../../etc/hosts, GET /_dashboard/../../secret, or GET /agents/../../../secret read files outside agents_root. Default bind is 127.0.0.1:8765, but dashboard __main__ already exposes operator-settable --host (default 127.0.0.1), so a 0.0.0.0 bind exposes the read on the LAN; loopback remains reachable via DNS rebinding or co-located SSRF. CWE-22 arbitrary file read.

**Flaw origin.** The uncontained Path joins were first written when dashboard/serve.py itself was created in the public root commit. At that snapshot _io.py had only atomic_write/atomic_append_jsonl/cleanup_stale_tempfiles (no safe_resolve_under) and exceptions.py had no PathTraversalError. The later tab-route commit only maps fixed names such as /activity -> activity.html through the same _serve_file helper; it does not introduce the untrusted-path mechanism. safe_resolve_under was added later for other modules and was not applied to this handler until the GHSA patch.

**BIC lifecycle.** introducer `151bd93d9cfb843673c52c290274615b3dd64936`; parent —; parent absence verified `True`; squash decomposed `False`; members `[]`.

**AI marker on BIC.** absent; BIC author/committer Dan Powers <dep0we@gmail.com>; cat-file headers have no parent and no Co-authored-by/Generated-with/Signed-off-by trailers. Body names Claude Code skill/ChatGPT/OpenAI API only as supported runtimes, not as commit authorship.

**Fix.** fix `ec474f458122c5c0ca718d0df3078c8080338b2c`; direct fix `ec474f458122c5c0ca718d0df3078c8080338b2c`.

**Reviewer-ready evidence.**

### 89. GHSA-mr52-gcmh-9959 — `alias-d4615d66f3492e391317db64`

- Repository: `cardboardpowered/cardboard`
- Official IDs: `CVE-2026-24794`, `GHSA-mr52-gcmh-9959`
- Selection: status `UNANALYZED`; score `159.774`; signals `repo_ai_commit_scan, ai_commits:26, unreviewed_advisory, ghsa_bundle, 2026`.
- Reproduction: bundle `.ai-slop/state/research-queue/round10/case-alias-d4615d66f3492e391317db64.json`; SHA-256 `f0af1a5f6e41b0ad0229d921644652f9a7544ab0b8a08e756841a8b7cd7be743`; base revision `1`; raw result `research/round10-top200-20260828/primary/w088.json`.
- Verdict: **NOT_AI**

**Vulnerability semantics.** Cardboard's public Bukkit World unloadChunk overloads funnel caller-controlled chunk coordinates into unloadChunk0. The vulnerable implementation obtains the NMS WorldChunk, requests an unload, drains queued chunk-manager tasks, and reports the result without first rejecting a chunk that is loaded/in use and without handling a null chunk reference. Thus an unload can be attempted while the chunk is active or unavailable; the first-party fix describes the resulting risk as server crashes, data corruption, and potential remote-code-execution vectors, while the advisory's scored impact is network-reachable high availability impact.

**Flaw origin.** Human-authored direct commit 11bb18aeec467e32f6bb8ae4ce04c4fa9a081d13 replaced unloadChunk0's harmless TODO/return-false stub with the unchecked nms.getChunk -> unloadChunkRequest -> executeQueuedTasks sequence in src/main/java/org/cardboardpowered/impl/world/WorldImpl.java. Later release-port commit 90055a82dbcd1ac2f2f771f7372595eee471c9e4 reintroduced the same body after a source rewrite, but it did not first create the flawed mechanism.

**BIC lifecycle.** introducer `11bb18aeec467e32f6bb8ae4ce04c4fa9a081d13`; parent `1c3a2061e0a4b9e1d09d87281a9babdd5fcdfed7`; parent absence verified `True`; squash decomposed `False`; members `[]`.

**AI marker on BIC.** absent — the exact BIC object (`git cat-file commit 11bb18aeec467e32f6bb8ae4ce04c4fa9a081d13`) has author Isaiah <isaiahpatton1@gmail.com>, committer Isaiah <isaiahpatton1@gmail.com>, and message `Fix blank World getEntities in 1.17`; it has no Co-Authored-By trailer, Generated-with trailer, bot identity, AI tool name, or other AI-attribution marker.

**Fix.** fix `f78fc7f35e0f83f2e3618aa06f3cae8532927abf`; direct fix `f78fc7f35e0f83f2e3618aa06f3cae8532927abf`.

**Reviewer-ready evidence.**

- First-party advisory https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-mr52-gcmh-9959 identifies CVE-2026-24794, WorldImpl.java, and `cardboard: before 1.21.4`; first-party PR https://github.com/CardboardPowered/cardboard/pull/506 identifies the missing in-use and null checks. First-party BIC page https://github.com/CardboardPowered/cardboard/commit/11bb18aeec467e32f6bb8ae4ce04c4fa9a081d13 shows parent 1c3a2061e0a4b9e1d09d87281a9babdd5fcdfed7 and the exact WorldImpl.java change. Local `git log -L` and global `git log -G 'unloadChunkRequest\s*\(x,\s*z\)' -- '*.java'` trace the mechanism to 11bb18aeec467e32f6bb8ae4ce04c4fa9a081d13; the latter also exposes later version-port reintroduction 90055a82dbcd1ac2f2f771f7372595eee471c9e4 rather than mistaking it for the origin. At the BIC, src/main/java/org/cardboardpowered/impl/world/WorldImpl.java lines 1893-1904 route all unloadChunk overloads to unloadChunk0, and lines 1907-1914 newly call nms.getChunk, unloadChunkRequest, executeQueuedTasks, and return the loaded-state result without either guard. Direct-parent tree verification (`git show 1c3a2061e0a4b9e1d09d87281a9babdd5fcdfed7:src/main/java/org/cardboardpowered/impl/world/WorldImpl.java` plus `git grep -F 'unloadChunkRequest(x, z)' 1c3a2061e0a4b9e1d09d87281a9babdd5fcdfed7 -- .../WorldImpl.java`) shows only `// TODO; return false` and no vulnerable call (grep has no match). `gradle.properties` at the BIC declares minecraft_version=1.17.1 and mod_version=1.17. With no repository tags (`git tag --list` is empty), versioned first-party branch tips provide the boundary check: origin/ver/1.18.2, ver/1.19.2, ver/1.19.4, ver/1.20, ver/1.20.4, ver/1.20.6, and ver/1.21 all contain the unchecked `unloadChunkRequest(x, z)` body, while their gradle.properties files identify versions 1.18.2 through 1.21/1.21.1. First-party fix https://github.com/CardboardPowered/cardboard/commit/f78fc7f35e0f83f2e3618aa06f3cae8532927abf has parent 979d2d38aeb64b01241735d73d26408c5ab88f83; parent grep finds the unload request but neither guard, whereas the fix adds `if (isChunkInUse(x, z)) return false` at WorldImpl.java:2035 and `if (chunk == null) return true` at lines 2040-2042. `git merge-base --is-ancestor 11bb18aeec467e32f6bb8ae4ce04c4fa9a081d13 f78fc7f35e0f83f2e3618aa06f3cae8532927abf` succeeds. `git branch -r --contains f78fc7f35e0f83f2e3618aa06f3cae8532927abf` includes origin/ver/1.21.4 and every later supported version branch but not ver/1.21 or older; merge 60d12f9e19f8b8437afab3407d75cc297337b362 carries the direct fix onto ver/1.21.4 as src/main/java/org/cardboardpowered/impl/world/CraftWorld.java, whose branch tip has the in-use guard at line 2030 and gradle.properties declares minecraft_version/mod_version 1.21.4. ### 90. GHSA-5j7r-7m6v-52v3 — `alias-9acecdbe83768cf660dad333`

The same affected script also eval'd selected Installomator label assignments, but the first-party issue and maintainer response identify the world-writable permission transition as the main enabling race, and the shipped boundary fix is the 777-to-755 change.

**Flaw origin.** The vulnerable permission block was first written in the 3.0 beta development history by dd0f4fcae4ce5951e541cb069ab5fe067e909575 in App-Auto-Patch-via-Dialog.zsh. ### 91. GHSA-q6v9-r226-v65f — `alias-35c0b7a943c1a4084769d1f8`

- Repository: `mtrudel/bandit`
- Official IDs: `CVE-2026-42788`, `GHSA-q6v9-r226-v65f`
- Selection: status `UNANALYZED`; score `159.61`; signals `repo_ai_commit_scan, ai_commits:9, reviewed_advisory, ghsa_bundle, 2026`.
- Reproduction: bundle `.ai-slop/state/research-queue/round10/case-alias-35c0b7a943c1a4084769d1f8.json`; SHA-256 `e612538914758906c0294f77da75d0b3aa703ab994f834911908cc0304fcf175`; base revision `1`; raw result `research/round10-top200-20260828/primary/w090.json`.
- Verdict: **NOT_AI**

**Vulnerability semantics.** Bandit's HTTP/2 connection handler appends each received chunk to state.buffer and repeatedly calls Frame.deserialize/2. The oversized-frame clause introduced to enforce max_frame_size destructured not only the 9-byte HTTP/2 header but also _payload::binary-size(length), so an attacker could announce a 24-bit length up to 16,777,215 bytes and keep the parser returning {:more, msg} until that entire body had accumulated. The length > max_frame_size guard therefore ran only after the excessive allocation, allowing unauthenticated h2/h2c peers to amplify per-connection buffering far beyond the negotiated 16 KiB default and cause memory-exhaustion denial of service.

**Flaw origin.** Commit f00dd69a5b2a4863be585907acd853c4ffd41399 added max_frame_size enforcement to lib/bandit/http2/frame.ex and passed state.connection.local_settings.max_frame_size from lib/bandit/http2/handler.ex, but wrote the rejecting clause with _payload::binary-size(length) before the length > max_frame_size guard. This made the newly introduced size check causally too late; the same commit's generic fallback continued to request more bytes for a header whose declared body was not yet complete.

**BIC lifecycle.** introducer `f00dd69a5b2a4863be585907acd853c4ffd41399`; parent `c7bfd639f8f07971090a6b8c009a8067589b9f44`; parent absence verified `True`; squash decomposed `False`; members `[]`.

**AI marker on BIC.** absent: the exact BIC commit object names author Mat Trudel <mat@geeky.net> and committer Mat Trudel <mat@geeky.net>; its message has no Co-Authored-By, Generated-with, or other AI trailer, and neither identity is a bot

**Fix.** fix `1e8e55966da9129016b73d32f0e1df4630e3b463`; direct fix `1e8e55966da9129016b73d32f0e1df4630e3b463`.

**Reviewer-ready evidence.**

- First-party advisory https://github.com/mtrudel/bandit/security/advisories/GHSA-q6v9-r226-v65f identifies lib/bandit/http2/frame.ex:23-65, explains that every oversized-frame check required payload::binary-size(length), demonstrates continued buffering after a 0xFFFFFF-length header, and names 1.11.0 as patched. Its rendered affected boundary is > 0.3.5 and < 1.11.0; the assigned bundle's normalized range says >= 0.3.5, but repository tags resolve the boundary unambiguously as described below.
- History search `git log main --full-history --reverse -p -L 22,75:lib/bandit/http2/frame.ex` and exact-string search `git log --all --reverse -S'_payload::binary-size(length)' -- lib/bandit/http2/frame.ex` identify f00dd69a5b2a4863be585907acd853c4ffd41399 as the first and smallest commit to write the flawed oversized-frame clause; the only later removal is the fix 1e8e55966da9129016b73d32f0e1df4630e3b463. The BIC is an ordinary one-parent commit, not a move, revert, merge, release commit, or squash aggregate.
- At f00dd69a5b2a4863be585907acd853c4ffd41399, `git blame -L 33,46 -- lib/bandit/http2/frame.ex` attributes the entire new oversized-frame clause to that commit, including line 40 `_payload::binary-size(length)` and line 43 `when length > max_frame_size`. `git blame -L 28,29 -- lib/bandit/http2/handler.ex` attributes line 28, which supplies `state.connection.local_settings.max_frame_size`, to the same BIC.
- Direct-parent verification: `git show c7bfd639f8f07971090a6b8c009a8067589b9f44:lib/bandit/http2/frame.ex` shows only deserialize/1, no max_frame_size argument, no length > max_frame_size guard, and no oversized-frame rejection clause. `git diff c7bfd639f8f07971090a6b8c009a8067589b9f44 f00dd69a5b2a4863be585907acd853c4ffd41399 -- lib/bandit/http2/frame.ex lib/bandit/http2/handler.ex` proves that the BIC added those exact vulnerable lines and wired the negotiated limit into the buffering path.

### 94. GHSA-c67r-gc9j-2qf7 — `alias-7aefdab51abb8a9f1125aa0b`

- Verdict: **NOT_AI**

**Vulnerability semantics.** Bandit's HTTP/1 parser preserved repeated header lines, but its Content-Length framing path selected only one content-length tuple through List.keyfind/3 and silently ignored every other line. A frontend that framed a request using a different duplicate value could forward body bytes that Bandit, using the selected shorter value, left on the keep-alive connection and parsed as a second request, allowing CL.CL request smuggling across frontend-only WAF, ACL, rate-limit, or audit boundaries.

**Flaw origin.** Commit e5270b1b19e9f3574aa0f87ec76851d66c38c0af first added Content-Length-based request-body framing in lib/bandit/http1_request.ex. It obtained the request length through a new generic get_header/3 helper implemented with List.keyfind(headers, header, 0), so the very first framing implementation consumed one Content-Length without validating that no duplicate line existed. Later refactors moved this same single-value mechanism into lib/bandit/http1/adapter.ex and then lib/bandit/headers.ex; they did not originate it.

**BIC lifecycle.** introducer `e5270b1b19e9f3574aa0f87ec76851d66c38c0af`; parent `d5989c8d8a806639c73d4294762192a7aba3c3ac`; parent absence verified `True`; squash decomposed `False`; members `[]`.

### 96. GHSA-q8ch-jx67-q52x — `alias-f94bebcf0e74bd2ed76c1c00`

- Repository: `apache/camel-k`
- Official IDs: `CVE-2026-45760`, `GHSA-q8ch-jx67-q52x`

- Verdict: **NOT_AI**

**Vulnerability semantics.** Cross-namespace authorization bypass/confused-deputy flaw: a user allowed to create a Camel K Build in a watched Kubernetes namespace could supply the serialized `operatorNamespace` value, which the privileged operator trusted as the namespace for builder-Pod creation, lookup, deletion, and security-context lookup. Pointing it at another namespace—including the operator namespace—crossed the caller's authorization boundary and let the caller control Pod generation there.

**Flaw origin.** Commit 6335618feabac9128f42c2d6ad2d3a289ed4e753 changed the builder-Pod namespace sink from the Build object's trusted metadata namespace (`build.Namespace`) to a new, user-serialized `Build.spec.operatorNamespace` field returned by `build.OperatorNamespace()`, without checking that the target namespace equaled the Build namespace or was otherwise authorized. Commit 5b00e5f7594dcdc22e5373102f1833ec32439d5a later renamed that accessor/field to `BuilderPodNamespace` and subsequent refactoring moved the value into builder task configuration, but those were continuity-preserving refactors, not the origin.

**BIC lifecycle.** introducer `6335618feabac9128f42c2d6ad2d3a289ed4e753`; parent `4c6f2a5d411ee6291eda5e36704eed835b8f24a1`; parent absence verified `True`; squash decomposed `False`; members `[]`.

**Fix.** fix `72aab0a2d2befb13856ce8a67bbe0ea1536aaade`; direct fix `222cdbd80481a4306c76cce66361f0dff07c18bf`.

### 97. GHSA-g5c4-g774-r8rq — `alias-4f97d3580c6c97848d20a8f3`

- Repository: `cerebrate-project/cerebrate`
- Official IDs: `CVE-2026-53901`, `GHSA-g5c4-g774-r8rq`

- Verdict: **NOT_AI**

**Vulnerability semantics.** The generic CRUD add handler created a new entity and marshalled attacker-controlled POST data, including an id, into that entity before save. A later guard inspected and removed id from the controller-options array $params, but __massageInput($params) independently rebuilt $input from $this->request->getData(); the attacker-controlled id therefore survived into patchEntity(), allowing an add endpoint to persist an attacker-chosen server-controlled identifier and potentially spoof objects, collide identifiers, or corrupt references.

**Flaw origin.** Commit 62c9050fb2c5fb0d351594dec8bbec645860940b first added app/src/Controller/Component/CRUDComponent.php and its generic add() data flow: on POST it passed $this->request->getData() directly to patchEntity() and then saved the new entity without excluding id. Commit a7348e5266b21f210d0d37eb397dbd52a5302659 later refactored the raw request read into __massageInput($params) without filtering id, and 7159034e9e1b2b9e0f61efeef2acce5651fd756e later added the ineffective unset($params['id']) guard. Those later commits preserved or attempted to mitigate the already-existing flaw; they did not first introduce the vulnerable request-to-entity sink.

**BIC lifecycle.** introducer `62c9050fb2c5fb0d351594dec8bbec645860940b`; parent `dccf9d5fd6c1ad13d5983a5c13ef41456551aa71`; parent absence verified `True`; squash decomposed `False`; members `[]`.

**Fix.** fix `aff1ca707c8f926d00cda3deb39ff9bf59cdf18e`; direct fix `aff1ca707c8f926d00cda3deb39ff9bf59cdf18e`.

**Reviewer-ready evidence.**

In the validated full-history clone, `git diff dccf9d5fd6c1ad13d5983a5c13ef41456551aa71 62c9050fb2c5fb0d351594dec8bbec645860940b -- app/src/Controller/Component/CRUDComponent.php` shows the file added from /dev/null and add() calling patchEntity($data, $this->request->getData()) before save; `git diff --name-status` shows that this BIC changed only that newly added file. `git ls-tree -r --name-only dccf9d5fd6c1ad13d5983a5c13ef41456551aa71 -- app/src/Controller/Component/CRUDComponent.php src/Controller/Component/CRUDComponent.php` returns no path, directly proving the vulnerable component and lines absent from the BIC parent. ### 98. GHSA-88x3-39g9-9frv — `alias-98cf9600bcfc8b17365972a8`

- Repository: `cerebrate-project/cerebrate`
- Official IDs: `CVE-2026-53912`, `GHSA-88x3-39g9-9frv`
- Selection: status `UNANALYZED`; score `159.502`; signals `repo_ai_commit_scan, ai_commits:25, unreviewed_advisory, ghsa_bundle, 2026`.
- Reproduction: bundle `.ai-slop/state/research-queue/round10/case-alias-98cf9600bcfc8b17365972a8.json`; SHA-256 `cbcd72fd956a9602f03c871f5eab2c0ad59ebe72b4ebd528c79163653be35da3`; base revision `1`; raw result `research/round10-top200-20260828/primary/w097.json`.
- Verdict: **NOT_AI**

**Vulnerability semantics.** With self-registration enabled, an unauthenticated registrant's submitted password was hashed and retained as Inbox.data.password so an administrator could later create the account. The generic inbox index and view paths serialized that JSON payload without redaction to HTML, JSON, and CSV consumers; after Inbox acquired AuditLogBehavior, the same nested credential could also be copied unredacted into audit-log changes. An authenticated user with the required inbox or audit-log privileges could therefore obtain a pending registrant's password hash for offline cracking.

**Flaw origin.** Commit 370ae3438e468f168f5793a720125e6d53943bd1 converted the earlier dummy registration handler into public self-registration and, in the same commit, added src/Controller/UsersController.php's password field to the inbox payload plus libraries/default/InboxProcessors/UserInboxProcessor.php's hashing and parent::create() save. The already-existing generic InboxController index()/view() returned Inbox entities without credential filtering. Commit 2e1ee2d064c07322d7f074160a6de9d5512e43f6 later attached AuditLogBehavior to Inbox, adding a second disclosure surface, but the credential-in-unredacted-inbox mechanism was already vulnerable from 370ae3438e468f168f5793a720125e6d53943bd1.

### 99. GHSA-ccc2-wrmm-mgwp — `alias-a2dab60c0b5aca6d53f0f6d8`

- Repository: `cerebrate-project/cerebrate`
- Official IDs: `CVE-2026-53911`, `GHSA-ccc2-wrmm-mgwp`
- Selection: status `UNANALYZED`; score `159.502`; signals `repo_ai_commit_scan, ai_commits:25, unreviewed_advisory, ghsa_bundle, 2026`.
- Reproduction: bundle `.ai-slop/state/research-queue/round10/case-alias-a2dab60c0b5aca6d53f0f6d8.json`; SHA-256 `1fb2520b074610e658d5b09525b3b4a6f1e268f9dc2aea8307b9da3f83a72661`; base revision `1`; raw result `research/round10-top200-20260828/primary/w098.json`.
- Verdict: **NOT_AI**

**Vulnerability semantics.** Cerebrate's generic CRUD edit flow loaded the entity selected by the route id, then passed the complete request body to CakePHP patchEntity(). For entities inheriting permissive mass-assignment defaults, a body-supplied id replaced that loaded entity's primary key; save() could consequently update a different same-type record than the route and authorization checks selected. UserSettingsController::edit was available to ordinary authenticated users, so a user could authorize against one of their own settings but redirect the write by supplying another setting's id. The same missing primary-key guard also exposed certain custom patchEntity flows.

**Flaw origin.** The smallest line-origin commit is 62c9050fb2c5fb0d351594dec8bbec645860940b. It created app/src/Controller/Component/CRUDComponent.php and first wrote edit() with Table->get($id), raw request->getData() passed to Table->patchEntity(), and Table->save($data), without removing id or restricting accessible fields. The base AppModel and affected entities such as UserSetting supplied no id-inaccessible override. Commit 44c60942c0d820ab0da4b08cced38ac2a602a825 later renamed that file at 100% similarity to src/Controller/Component/CRUDComponent.php; it did not originate the flaw. A later custom-path instance was added in aa83b1aa370dfdbdc35b06b0279fedbeb1e3fe7d, but it postdates the generic vulnerable sink and is not the earliest BIC.

**BIC lifecycle.** introducer `62c9050fb2c5fb0d351594dec8bbec645860940b`; parent `dccf9d5fd6c1ad13d5983a5c13ef41456551aa71`; parent absence verified `True`; squash decomposed `False`; members `[]`.

**AI marker on BIC.** absent: the exact BIC commit object names author and committer iglocska <andras.iklody@gmail.com>; its message has no Co-Authored-By, Generated-with, bot identity, AI trailer, or other AI-attribution marker.

**Fix.** fix `b3c8f951b0634f05691339512ef06cc261afecaf`; direct fix `b3c8f951b0634f05691339512ef06cc261afecaf`.

**Reviewer-ready evidence.**

- First-party patched-release evidence: https://github.com/cerebrate-project/cerebrate/releases/tag/v1.37 calls v1.37 a security release and states that a POST-body id could redirect add/edit save() to an unrelated record, that /user_settings/edit was reachable by any authenticated user, and that the repair strips id in CRUDComponent::add()/edit() and blocks it globally in AppModel::$_accessible.
- Advisory evidence: https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-ccc2-wrmm-mgwp (CVE-2026-53911) describes Cerebrate before 1.37, the affected permissive entities User, Role, UserSetting, LocalTool, PermissionLimitation, and EnumerationCollection, and links the first-party fix https://github.com/cerebrate-project/cerebrate/commit/b3c8f951b0634f05691339512ef06cc261afecaf.
- Line-origin evidence: git log -L over src/Controller/Component/CRUDComponent.php follows edit() through the path history to 62c9050fb2c5fb0d351594dec8bbec645860940b, whose new app/src/Controller/Component/CRUDComponent.php contains Table->get($id), Table->patchEntity($data, $this->request->getData()), and Table->save($data). git show confirms this is a one-parent, new-file commit, not a move, merge, backport, revert, or squash aggregate.
- Direct-parent evidence: git ls-tree -r --name-only dccf9d5fd6c1ad13d5983a5c13ef41456551aa71 -- app/src/Controller/Component/CRUDComponent.php src/Controller/Component/CRUDComponent.php returns no path. Thus the vulnerable CRUD edit lines are absent from the BIC's immediate parent tree. The later path change is independently identified as R100 by git log --follow: 44c60942c0d820ab0da4b08cced38ac2a602a825 renamed app/src/Controller/Component/CRUDComponent.php to src/Controller/Component/CRUDComponent.php.
- Attack-path evidence immediately before the fix: b5952d8e0da73e66ae74faa3fe58c22326d17292:src/Controller/UserSettingsController.php checks ownership of the route-selected UserSetting, then calls CRUD->edit($id); b5952d8e0da73e66ae74faa3fe58c22326d17292:src/Model/Entity/UserSetting.php is an empty AppModel subclass, and that parent version of AppModel has no $_accessible id guard. The parent CRUD edit then patches the loaded entity with the unfiltered input before saving.
- Custom-flow lifecycle evidence: git log -L for src/Controller/MetaTemplatesController.php shows aa83b1aa370dfdbdc35b06b0279fedbeb1e3fe7d first added migrateOldMetaTemplateToNewestVersionForEntity(), including request->getData(), patchEntity(), and save() without an id guard; b3c8f951b0634f05691339512ef06cc261afecaf adds unset($inputData['id']) there.
- Fix evidence: b3c8f951b0634f05691339512ef06cc261afecaf (parent b5952d8e0da73e66ae74faa3fe58c22326d17292) inserts the post-beforeMarshal id removal in CRUDComponent::edit(), moves the add() guard after callbacks, removes id in the MetaTemplates custom flow, and adds AppModel::$_accessible = ['*' => true, 'id' => false]. It is therefore both the advisory-linked fix and the direct source fix.
- Version-boundary evidence: git tag --contains 62c9050fb2c5fb0d351594dec8bbec645860940b includes every release tag from v0.1 through v1.36 (and later tags), while git tag --contains b3c8f951b0634f05691339512ef06cc261afecaf begins at v1.37. v1.36 resolves to 6d0160ded30f7c0f94cc3d7af7efe26202316d40 and lacks the fix; v1.37 resolves to 9a308a10fd0958f59b801d66c50aa6e369276c4e and contains the direct fix through its develop-side ancestry. This matches the first-party 'before 1.37' / fixed-in-1.37 boundary.
- BIC-only AI evidence: git cat-file commit 62c9050fb2c5fb0d351594dec8bbec645860940b shows human author and committer iglocska <andras.iklody@gmail.com>, a signed commit, and only the subject/body 'new: [CRUD] crud component added' plus two ordinary bullets; no AI marker or attribution trailer occurs in that commit object. AI assistance disclosed for the 2026 discovery/fix is not evidence about the 2020 BIC.

**Reasoning.** The vulnerability is a route/body identity mismatch: authorization and lookup use the route id, but mass assignment lets the body replace the entity primary key before persistence. Vulnerability-first history tracing identifies the first written generic mechanism in 62c9050fb2c5fb0d351594dec8bbec645860940b, rather than the later R100 path move, later edits, the secondary MetaTemplates sink, or the 2026 repair. Its direct parent has neither historical nor current CRUDComponent path, proving the vulnerable lines absent. The BIC predates and is contained in the first v0.1 tag and all releases through v1.36. The direct patch b3c8f951b0634f05691339512ef06cc261afecaf is absent from the v1.36 boundary and contained by v1.37, matching the advisory and the project's v1.37 security release. Finally, the exact BIC commit object has no AI authorship, co-authorship, bot, or generation marker. Later AI assistance in finding or fixing the issue cannot attribute the BIC, so the causal verdict is NOT_AI.

### 100. GHSA-7ff3-w2cq-gmpq — `alias-f023f924fd9f60a72dcafabb`

- Repository: `penpot/penpot`
- Official IDs: `CVE-2026-17613`, `GHSA-7ff3-w2cq-gmpq`

- Verdict: **NOT_AI**

**Vulnerability semantics.** The ::import-binfile RPC accepted an optional, caller-controlled file-id for an in-place v3 import but authorized only the separately supplied project-id. The overwrite branch fetched the target file by id alone, imported attacker-controlled content with the caller's project-id, and updated the file row by the supplied target id, so an authenticated user who could edit their own project could overwrite and re-parent a victim file without permission on that file. The advisory's WebSocket-subscription language describes a related authorization omission, but the named import-binfile flaw and the BIC/fix fields here trace the file takeover mechanism.

**Flaw origin.** 37cec8891f44b0c320006193783d8648d3f32d0f is the smallest commit that created the vulnerable import path end to end: it added optional :file-id to schema:import-binfile, destructured and copied it into ::bfc/file-id, added import-file-and-overwrite* with an id-only get-minimal-file lookup, and made save-file! update rather than insert while preserving the caller-supplied project-id. Its direct parent had neither the external file-id parameter nor the overwrite branch and only created new imported files.

**BIC lifecycle.** introducer `37cec8891f44b0c320006193783d8648d3f32d0f`; parent `fd62141c04817c2ae86d10ad41b130fe616cf789`; parent absence verified `True`; squash decomposed `False`; members `[]`.

**AI marker on BIC.** absent — the raw BIC commit object names author Andrey Antukh <niwi@niwi.nz> and committer Andrey Antukh <niwi@niwi.nz>; after the headers it contains only the subject ':tada: Add inplace binfile import support' and no body, Co-Authored-By trailer, Generated-with trailer, bot identity, or other AI marker.

**Fix.** fix `9242556da6b87d646d766385c24575cc71a1c6a5`; direct fix `9242556da6b87d646d766385c24575cc71a1c6a5`.

**Reviewer-ready evidence.**

- Advisory: https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-7ff3-w2cq-gmpq identifies CVE-2026-17613/GHSA-7ff3-w2cq-gmpq and the unchecked optional file-id; the linked technical advisory https://vokecyber.com/research/cve-2026-17613-penpot-cross-team-file-takeover describes the one-request overwrite/re-parent attack. BIC: first-party commit https://github.com/penpot/penpot/commit/37cec8891f44b0c320006193783d8648d3f32d0f. `git log -L 124,161:backend/src/app/rpc/commands/binfile.clj 37cec8891f44b0c320006193783d8648d3f32d0f` and exact-string `git log --all --reverse -F -S'[:file-id {:optional true} ::sm/uuid]'` show that 37cec8891f44b0c320006193783d8648d3f32d0f first added the optional parameter and passed it into overwrite configuration in backend/src/app/rpc/commands/binfile.clj:124-161. The same BIC added the id-only target lookup and overwrite transaction in backend/src/app/binfile/v3.clj:912-935, imported the archive under the caller-supplied project at backend/src/app/binfile/v3.clj:710-765 (the project assignment is line 757), and updated the existing row by id in backend/src/app/binfile/common.clj:516-535/558-569. Direct-parent proof: `git grep` for the exact schema entry, `assoc ::bfc/file-id file-id`, and `import-file-and-overwrite` against fd62141c04817c2ae86d10ad41b130fe616cf789 over those two source files returned no matches; the BIC diff shows the parent accepted only project-id/version/file and followed the new-file import path. Version boundary: `git tag --contains 37cec8891f44b0c320006193783d8648d3f32d0f` starts with the 2.10.0 release family; 2.9.0 has neither vulnerable line, while first affected RC 2.10.0-RC1 (tag 2a2735cd67994857d1cbdfbff148c41220a53f1e, 2025-09-01) and first affected stable 2.10.0 (tag d4b7f231c7a8c0ea4abdd271f32531e8b5e792e0, 2025-09-29) contain the BIC. This repository history therefore does not support the research article's claimed 'v1.20 onward' product-version boundary. Fix: first-party issue https://github.com/penpot/penpot/issues/10993 and PR https://github.com/penpot/penpot/pull/10994 lead to direct patch https://github.com/penpot/penpot/commit/461227fe16c3c188c1c88eb401205578cdd72caf and merged develop fix https://github.com/penpot/penpot/commit/9242556da6b87d646d766385c24575cc71a1c6a5; both remove file-id handling and close the RPC schema. Neither fix is contained by any tag. First-party releases https://github.com/penpot/penpot/releases/tag/2.17.0 and https://github.com/penpot/penpot/releases/tag/2.17.2 remain vulnerable: `git grep` finds both vulnerable lines in 2.17.0, 2.17.1, 2.17.2, and 2.18.0-RC1, including 2.17.2 tag 1d2c37e52c733f74017d90b0fd1ae2d074a5c33d dated 2026-08-27. Thus source is fixed on develop after 9242556da6b87d646d766385c24575cc71a1c6a5, but there is no tagged fixed-version boundary in the clone as of 2026-08-28. AI check: `git cat-file -p 37cec8891f44b0c320006193783d8648d3f32d0f` produced the exact author, committer, parent, and subject stated in ai_marker and no trailers. direct_fix_sha aligned to the landed fix 9242556da6b87d646d766385c24575cc71a1c6a5 (reconciliation 2026-08-29): the previously named commit 461227fe16c3c188c1c88eb401205578cdd72caf is a sibling branch/backport commit, not an ancestor of the landed fix (merge-base verified).

**Reasoning.** The causal unit is not the older generic import RPC: before fd62141c04817c2ae86d10ad41b130fe616cf789's child, imports targeted a project the caller was authorized to edit and created new files. Commit 37cec8891f44b0c320006193783d8648d3f32d0f simultaneously exposed an arbitrary existing file id and implemented the id-only overwrite path. Because the authorization call remained scoped to project-id, an attacker could pass their own authorized project plus a victim file id; the BIC then loaded that victim row by id, wrote attacker archive data, and persisted the attacker's project-id, causing both destruction and takeover. Exact -S and -L history identify this commit rather than a later refactor, release, or fix, and direct-parent tree search proves the vulnerable mechanism absent. Tag ancestry places the first affected stable release at 2.10.0 and confirms that the latest inspected stable 2.17.2 is still affected. The original remediation commit 461227fe16c3c188c1c88eb401205578cdd72caf was reproduced as 9242556da6b87d646d766385c24575cc71a1c6a5 on develop, removing the dangerous parameter/use and closing the schema, but no release tag contains either fix. Finally, attribution is decided only from the BIC's raw commit object: it is a human-authored/human-committed object with no AI marker, so the closed causal verdict is NOT_AI.

### 102. GHSA-g8mq-qr24-3qv3 — `alias-34fbdb847d02acf7e1b08144`

- Repository: `openpanel-dev/openpanel`
- Official IDs: `CVE-2026-77768`, `GHSA-g8mq-qr24-3qv3`

- Verdict: **NOT_AI**

**Vulnerability semantics.** An authenticated caller could invoke report.get with only an arbitrary reportId. protectedProcedure authenticated the caller, but enforceAccess checked project or organization membership only when raw input contained a projectId or organizationId key, so this input triggered no tenant authorization. The handler then passed the attacker-controlled UUID to the unscoped getReportById service, whose Prisma findUnique selected solely by id and returned the transformed report, disclosing another organization's projectId, event series, filters, breakdowns, formulas, and other saved configuration.

**Flaw origin.** PR #211 member commit 3540c8b83a57ca2f926725158defce34bf304fec first connected the pre-existing unscoped getReportById helper to a new protected report.get RPC whose schema carried reportId but no access-bearing projectId or organizationId. That nine-line endpoint in packages/trpc/src/routers/report.ts:138-146 completed the vulnerable cross-tenant path; its direct parent had neither the endpoint nor its getReportById import. GitHub later squash-merged the PR as 81a7e5d62ec29ad3bf971610d5243a11a62a603d, but the reconstructable member commit, not the aggregate, is the smallest BIC.

**BIC lifecycle.** introducer `3540c8b83a57ca2f926725158defce34bf304fec`; parent `68d194e8c6a1dd52913fb5fed4c01aa2fc27d823`; parent absence verified `True`; squash decomposed `True`; members `["3540c8b83a57ca2f926725158defce34bf304fec", "6b2efdd19bb044be0c7d0bdde9db0a599cbe2466"]`.

**Fix.** fix `0a51b6805eed0b3da8376175acd5fa3d26819cb6`; direct fix `0a51b6805eed0b3da8376175acd5fa3d26819cb6`.

**Reviewer-ready evidence.**

- First-party advisory https://github.com/Openpanel-dev/openpanel/security/advisories/GHSA-9x7c-f87x-2243 identifies report.get, packages/trpc/src/trpc.ts enforceAccess, and packages/db/src/services/reports.service.ts getReportById; it declares OpenPanel API 2.2.0 affected and 2.3.0 patched and records live validation at e8a0602cda5a4d4b463f11d298a1b078c446bf33. At the reconstructed BIC, packages/trpc/src/routers/report.ts:138-146 accepts only reportId and returns getReportById(reportId); packages/trpc/src/trpc.ts:91-123 checks access only inside has('projectId', rawInput) and has('organizationId', rawInput); packages/db/src/services/reports.service.ts:84-95 performs db.report.findUnique({where:{id}}) and returns transformReport. `git log -L 184,192:packages/trpc/src/routers/report.ts a45bdb0f9372d8d4ef61f313b41142b63a2140e2` led to squash commit 81a7e5d62ec29ad3bf971610d5243a11a62a603d (PR #211). `git ls-remote origin refs/pull/211/head` resolved 330321405d2ba207cb1672d1d38a4f0cdac85ad8; that head and 81a7e5d62ec29ad3bf971610d5243a11a62a603d have the identical tree bd678581f1cc78a42ff07619c4bd7051c7c69cbb. In the PR-member history for report.ts, 3540c8b83a57ca2f926725158defce34bf304fec adds the entire vulnerable nine-line handler, while later member 6b2efdd19bb044be0c7d0bdde9db0a599cbe2466 adds layout procedures and leaves that handler unchanged. A zero-context diff from direct parent 68d194e8c6a1dd52913fb5fed4c01aa2fc27d823 to 3540c8b83a57ca2f926725158defce34bf304fec shows the handler and import as additions, and `git grep` for both `get: protectedProcedure` and `return getReportById(reportId)` in the direct-parent report.ts produced no match. The direct first-party fix is https://github.com/Openpanel-dev/openpanel/commit/0a51b6805eed0b3da8376175acd5fa3d26819cb6: packages/trpc/src/routers/report.ts changes report.get to load the report, reject a missing report, call getProjectAccess with ctx.session.userId and report.projectId, reject absent access, and only then return the report. Version cross-check: the repository has no 2.2.0/2.3.0 git tag, but publisher registry records at https://hub.docker.com/v2/repositories/lindesvard/openpanel-api/tags/2.2.0 and https://hub.docker.com/v2/repositories/lindesvard/openpanel-api/tags/2.3.0 exist, and their BuildKit provenance names this GitHub repository and source revisions ed8b5c667e6dd7f7b960c60ea5be9ce8c11ad8e1 and 373be136190aa73debd4508fa4ac05619ce04a53 respectively. Revision ed8b5c667e6dd7f7b960c60ea5be9ce8c11ad8e1 contains the vulnerable direct return at report.ts:175-183, contains squash 81a7e5d62ec29ad3bf971610d5243a11a62a603d, and predates the fix; revision 373be136190aa73debd4508fa4ac05619ce04a53 contains 0a51b6805eed0b3da8376175acd5fa3d26819cb6 and has the access check at report.ts:197-215. The aggregate 81a7e5d62ec29ad3bf971610d5243a11a62a603d transported those lines to main and is present before the 2.2.0 image revision. Fix 0a51b6805eed0b3da8376175acd5fa3d26819cb6 closes the exact gap by deriving projectId from the fetched report and authorizing that project before disclosure; the 2.3.0 image revision contains this fix and the corrected code. Because the smallest BIC's own commit object has human author and committer identities and no AI authorship, co-authorship, generation trailer, or bot marker, later PR review automation and any evidence outside that BIC object do not attribute the root cause to AI, so the closed verdict is NOT_AI.

### 103. GHSA-fhw4-v2hr-j5m2 — `alias-47f0ad68fdab15129b790c82`

- Repository: `feed-mob/fm-mcp-servers`
